contexts.description: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol surface that exposes Personas as A2A-compatible agents over HTTP. Defines the on-the-wire request/response shapes for the A2A gateway, enabling other AI systems to call Personas agents via the standard A2A protocol. Currently implements the server (inbound) side; outbound A2A client is planned.
contexts.name: a2a-gateway

contexts.description: Multi-layer access control enforcing scope, path safety, platform rules, and tier gating. The scope_enforcement module checks whether a persona's requested action falls within its declared capability scope; path_safety validates file paths against allowed directories; platform_rules applies OS-specific restrictions; tier controls feature availability per subscription level; desktop_security gates which native app bridges may be invoked.
contexts.name: access-control

contexts.description: Handles user account lifecycle and cloud data synchronisation: Google OAuth sign-in/sign-out flows, telemetry opt-in/opt-out toggle, and manual app update checking with version history. When authenticated, renders a cloud sync dashboard showing per-table sync state, last sync timestamp, total rows synced across all tracked tables, and a Sync Now trigger. Calls the cloudSync API module which maps to a Supabase-backed Rust sync writer. Depends on the app's auth store for session state.
contexts.name: account-cloud-sync

contexts.description: Diagnostic HTTP bridge for the adoption / persona-layout UI surface. Provides AdoptionBridge with helpers to query the AdoptionWizardModal DOM, inspect scroll metrics via eval round-trips, click layout tabs by text, and check whether the credential modal is open. Used by the adoption-persona-layout spec.
contexts.name: adoption-bridge

contexts.description: Per-persona activity log tab showing a chronological list of events (executions, health checks, config changes) with filtering and header. ActivityModals provides detail overlays for individual events. activityTypes centralises the event-type taxonomy used for filtering and display.
contexts.name: agent-activity

contexts.description: Slices for the agent chat feature, covering both the foreground interactive chat session and background autonomous chat polling. The mini-player slice provides floating-window state for agents running while the user navigates away.
contexts.name: agent-chat-state

contexts.description: Slice managing agent execution lifecycle — initiating runs, tracking output lines, handling cancellations, and maintaining a pipeline trace with middleware stages. Keeps a capped snapshot ring of completed executions and integrates with the execution sink for streaming terminal output.
contexts.name: agent-execution-state

contexts.description: Per-persona health monitoring tab: runs a health check (useHealthCheck) that evaluates assertions and surfaces issues as HealthIssueCards, shows an overall health score, a digest panel with prefetching and scheduled digest refreshes, a watch toggle, and a one-click apply-fix action. gradeColors and statusConfig centralise severity presentation.
contexts.name: agent-health

contexts.description: Slices supporting the Agent Lab feature for offline experimentation, A/B matrix builds, manual test runs, tool configuration, budget limits, and scheduled health checks. The lab slice fetches historical runs; matrix build slice coordinates multi-model variant generation.
contexts.name: agent-lab-quality-state

contexts.description: Provides hooks for browsing, selecting, and enriching agent/persona data in the UI. Covers recently-used agents, favorites, hover-prefetch for detail panels, a picklist selector, execution annotations overlaid on agent cards, and a shared persona-name lookup map. These hooks bridge the agent store and the persona list/card surfaces.
contexts.name: agent-list-hooks

contexts.description: Repositories for persona memories — long-term facts and context that agents accumulate across sessions. Includes the main memories store, claim/proposal workflow for reviewing and promoting new memories, and memory recall logic for surfacing relevant memories during execution.
contexts.name: agent-memory-repo

contexts.description: Repository for the core Persona entity — CRUD for AI agent persona definitions, settings, saved views, design conversations, and curation scheduling. Personas are the fundamental unit of the app, representing AI agents with configured tools, connectors, system prompts, and behavioral settings.
contexts.name: agent-persona-repo

contexts.description: Zustand slice managing the full lifecycle of persona entities — listing, selecting, creating, updating, duplicating, and deleting personas. Caches sub-resources (tools, triggers, subscriptions) per persona ID and exposes a derived selectedPersona computed from the canonical personas list merged with the detail cache.
contexts.name: agent-persona-state

contexts.description: Git checkpointing and deterministic dream-replay for execution debugging and recovery. The git_checkpoint module creates per-stage commits on a run-specific branch enabling rollback; dream_replay reconstructs execution state frame-by-frame from stored trace spans for VCR-style time-travel debugging without consuming LLM tokens; context_fidelity manages graded upstream-context injection in pipeline fan-in nodes.
contexts.name: agent-session-replay

contexts.description: Per-persona settings tab housing assertion configuration (what the persona guarantees), a settings status bar showing configuration completeness, and a composite PersonaSettingsTab layout. Assertions define behavioral contracts that are checked during health evaluations.
contexts.name: agent-settings

contexts.description: Top-level Zustand store that composes all agent-domain slices into a single persisted store. It wires persona selection, chat mode, and active chat session ID into localStorage via a deduped JSON storage adapter. Migration logic handles renamed chatMode values across releases.
contexts.name: agent-store-root

contexts.description: Test-automation harness commands — the test-automation HTTP server bridge (`:17320`) for MCP-driven UI tests, and a synthesize-review command that generates structured code-review outputs from execution transcripts. Only compiled under the `test-automation` Cargo feature.
contexts.name: agent-testing

contexts.description: Use-case management tab for a persona: lists, creates, and details use-cases (discrete tasks a persona handles). Provides layout views, per-use-case detail panel with model/channel/fixture selection, a recipes-prototype tile grid for visual use-case composition, and hooks for toggling capabilities and manually triggering runs.
contexts.name: agent-use-cases

contexts.description: Conversational AI-driven design tab embedded in the persona editor. Guides the user through analysis, refining, previewing, and applying phases that generate or update a persona's prompt and parameters via an LLM conversation. Manages multi-phase state (analyzing, refining, preview, applied, error) and displays example input/output pairs.
contexts.name: ai-design-tab

contexts.description: AI meta-orchestration layer — Director (meta-persona that reviews and scores execution outputs), Autopilot (auto-run policy engine), BYOM (bring-your-own-model configuration), and Twin (AI-generated digital twin for simulated user testing). These commands govern how and when AI runs without human intervention.
contexts.name: ai-director

contexts.description: Abstraction layer for AI model providers consumed by the execution engine. The provider module defines the provider trait; the claude submodule implements the Anthropic Claude API client used for inline (non-CLI) calls such as design feasibility checks and triage evaluations, separate from the primary CLI-based execution path.
contexts.name: ai-provider-layer

contexts.description: Multi-strategy self-healing system that diagnoses and recovers failed persona executions. The healing_orchestrator implements a precedence tree (failover → rule-based retry → AI healing → auto-rollback); ai_healing resumes the original Claude session to diagnose and apply fixes in dev mode; healing_timeline tracks the history of healing episodes and their outcomes.
contexts.name: ai-self-healing

contexts.description: Fuses clipboard, file-watcher, and app-focus desktop signals into a rolling context window for ambient persona awareness. The ambient_context module maintains a VecDeque of ContextEvents and resolves sensory policies; the signal repo persists ambient events; clipboard_monitor and clipboard_error_detector watch the clipboard; file_watcher tracks file-system changes; app_focus tracks foreground application; context_rules evaluates persona-declared sensory policies against the signal stream.
contexts.name: ambient-desktop-signals

contexts.api_surface: trackActivationStep(step, ordinal, installId) — routes through active AnalyticsSink.conversion
contexts.description: Activation-funnel tracking that fires a `ConversionEvent` exactly once per install milestone (persona created, first execution completed, sharing, import). Deduplicates against persisted install state so each step is reported at most once regardless of how many sessions occur. Feeds the growth funnel metrics (activation rate, time-to-value, K-factor) without polluting the higher-noise nav/interaction event stream.
contexts.name: analytics-activation

contexts.api_surface: AnalyticsSink interface (feature, interaction, session, conversion); setAnalyticsSink / applyTelemetrySink for runtime backend swap
contexts.description: Declarative navigation-usage analytics that auto-tracks every section and tab visit without a hand-maintained map. Subscribes to Zustand nav stores, emits structured `feature_visit` events through the pluggable `AnalyticsSink` abstraction, accumulates per-session counts, and flushes a single `session_summary` (visited + ignored) on `beforeunload`. The `navCatalog` drives coverage so adding a new tab to the store and listing it in the catalog is sufficient — no instrumentation code to write.
contexts.name: analytics-nav-tracking

contexts.description: Centralizes animation presets and a shared requestAnimationFrame engine for the UI. The RAF engine interpolates all registered spring targets in a single callback, writing directly to DOM refs to avoid React reconciliation overhead. Framer Motion presets and CSS duration classes are also exported here for consistent motion across components.
contexts.name: animation-motion

contexts.description: Vitest unit tests for the `src/api` IPC bridge layer, covering the most critical command surfaces: credentials, enums, events, executions, memories, messages, observability, personas, settings, system, and triggers. These tests validate the typed wrappers and serialization contracts between the React frontend and Tauri backend without requiring a running desktop binary.
contexts.name: api-bridge-tests

contexts.api_surface: createExternalApiKey, listExternalApiKeys, revokeExternalApiKey, deleteExternalApiKey, listApiKeyAudit; revokePairing; probeMcpServer (http://127.0.0.1:9420)
contexts.description: Manages API keys that third-party MCP clients use to authenticate against the local HTTP management server (port 9420). Handles full key lifecycle: creation with scoped permissions and optional expiry, one-time plaintext reveal dialog, soft revocation with audit trail, hard deletion, stale-key detection, and per-key audit log drawer. Also manages origin-bound 'Connected Apps' (cloud application OAuth-style pairings) and an MCP server liveness status panel. Depends on the external_api_keys and pairing command modules in Rust.
contexts.name: api-key-management

contexts.api_surface: proxy_request (Tauri command), query_database (Tauri command), list_resources (Tauri command)
contexts.description: Credential-authenticated HTTP proxy and resource access layer: proxies arbitrary HTTP requests through a credential's auth strategy with per-credential token-bucket rate limiting and aggregate latency/error metrics; provides the unified Capability trait for DB queries (Supabase, Neon, Upstash, PlanetScale) and resource-picker listing (repos, projects, tables). All three surfaces share the same resolve-credential → execute → audit-log pattern.
contexts.name: api-proxy-access

contexts.description: Application settings, initial setup, and IPC authentication infrastructure. Settings CRUD persists user preferences; setup handles first-launch bootstrapping; auth enforces IPC token validation before privileged commands. Also the commands module root.
contexts.name: app-settings

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_setting, set_setting, check_cli_readiness, install_component
contexts.description: Hooks for reading and persisting application settings: a generic app-setting accessor, granular density/layout-density preferences, engine capability detection, CLI readiness checks, auto-installer and auto-updater flows, formatted-date helpers, and settings-page utilities. These hooks wrap the settings Tauri commands and surface values from the settings store to components.
contexts.name: app-settings-hooks

contexts.description: Low-level application-state hooks shared across features: attention management for focus trapping, step-progress tracking for multi-step flows, a wizard state reducer, a slice-error aggregator, the Tauri event subscription primitive, and the public re-export index for the entire hooks package. These are cross-cutting primitives with no single domain owner.
contexts.name: app-state-hooks

contexts.api_surface: getAppSetting / setAppSetting (theme, density, language, timezone, brightness)
contexts.description: Manages all visual customisation for the application: language/locale selection with lazy-chunked bundle loading, UI density (compact/comfortable/spacious), text size, timezone for relative timestamps, display brightness, WCAG-annotated theme selection with hover previews, and a full custom-theme palette editor. Theme choices and density/brightness overrides are persisted through the app_settings Tauri command layer. Provides the ThemePreview and AppearanceThemeHoverPreview components used inline by other settings surfaces.
contexts.name: appearance-settings

contexts.description: Three.js-based 3D model viewer embedded in the gallery for previewing GLB/GLTF and other 3D asset formats. Renders models with orbit controls and lighting directly in the browser.
contexts.name: artist-3d-viewer

contexts.api_surface: artistListAssets, artistScanFolder, artistImportAsset, artistDeleteAsset, artistRenameAsset, artistUpdateTags, artistGetDefaultFolder, artistEnsureFolders, artistReadLocalImage
contexts.description: React hooks for loading, scanning, importing, tagging, renaming, and deleting artist assets from the local file system via Tauri IPC. Manages loading/scanning state, syncs the default folder from Tauri, and provides local image data-URL resolution with module-level cache invalidation.
contexts.name: artist-asset-hooks

contexts.description: HTTP bridge wrapper specialised for the Artist plugin, mirroring the companion-bridge shape. Provides ArtistBridge with typed helpers for navigating Artist tabs (blender, gallery, media-studio), reading composition names, and applying starter templates. Used exclusively by artist smoke and cycle specs.
contexts.name: artist-bridge

contexts.description: Canvas-based real-time composition preview that renders the current timeline state at the playback cursor position. Composites video thumbnails, images, and title overlays scaled to the canvas. Exposes a captureThumbnail() handle for the persistence layer to auto-generate composition thumbnails on save.
contexts.name: artist-composition-preview

contexts.description: React hooks powering the Creative Studio: Blender MCP status checking and installation, streaming creative session management (send prompt, cancel, clear output), and connector readiness detection for image-gen services. Bridges the UI to Tauri IPC commands for Blender and creative sessions.
contexts.name: artist-creative-hooks

contexts.description: Blender MCP integration panel for AI-assisted 3D creation. Shows Blender and blender-mcp install status, connected image-gen connectors (Leonardo AI, Gemini), a streaming CLI-backed creative session chat, session history, and a collapsible reference mood board. Users describe creative goals; the session runs them through available tools.
contexts.name: artist-creative-studio

contexts.api_surface: artistListAssets, artistScanFolder, artistImportAsset, artistDeleteAsset, artistRenameAsset, artistUpdateTags
contexts.description: Image and 3D model gallery for browsing, managing, and tagging AI-generated or imported creative assets. Supports 2D/3D mode toggle, search, sort, date-based grouping, folder scanning, and a drag-to-reference-board handoff to Creative Studio. Assets can be bulk-selected, tagged, renamed, deleted, and sent to Media Studio.
contexts.name: artist-gallery

contexts.api_surface: artistSaveComposition, artistLoadComposition, artistListRecentCompositions, artistExportComposition, artistFfmpegStatus, artistProbeMedia, artistReadAudioWaveform, artistVideoThumbnail
contexts.description: React hooks for Media Studio non-UI logic: composition state machine with 80-step undo/redo history and coalescing (useMediaStudio), file-persistence with MRU list and auto-thumbnail on save (useMediaStudioPersistence), FFmpeg binary detection (useFfmpegDetect), export progress tracking over IPC events (useMediaExport), media file picker via Tauri dialogs (useMediaFilePicker), audio waveform computation (useAudioWaveform), and video thumbnail generation (useVideoThumbnails).
contexts.name: artist-media-hooks

contexts.description: Non-linear video composition editor with a multi-lane timeline for video, audio, image, text beats, and title overlays. The root page orchestrates all sub-systems: composition state management with undo/redo, FFmpeg detection, media import, playback, export, and Gallery-to-MediaStudio asset handoff. Defines all timeline item types and composition schema.
contexts.name: artist-media-studio-core

contexts.description: Media Studio playback engine and controls. Implements a requestAnimationFrame-based virtual playback clock (PlaybackEngine) for scrubbing the composition preview, looping, and seeking without relying on a DOM media element. PlaybackControls exposes play/pause/stop/loop/seek and shows current time and total duration.
contexts.name: artist-playback

contexts.description: End-to-end specs for the Artist plugin: smoke test verifying all three tabs (Blender, Gallery, Media Studio) render their page wrappers and lazy-load content, plus drive-cycle feature tests for Media Studio composition flows.
contexts.name: artist-plugin-e2e

contexts.description: Top-level shell for the Artist plugin that routes between three sub-tabs (Creative Studio, Gallery, Media Studio) driven by the `artistTab` state in systemStore. Provides the shared ContentHeader across subtab switches and lazy-loads each sub-page. Entry point for the entire Artist feature area.
contexts.name: artist-plugin-shell

contexts.description: Render plan computation layer that translates the in-memory composition into an IR (Intermediate Representation) list of FFmpeg operations. Validates clip paths, detects gaps/overlaps, computes transition sequences, and surfaces warnings. The render plan is consumed by both the export path and the composition preview.
contexts.name: artist-render-plan

contexts.description: Visual timeline editor UI components: the scrollable multi-lane panel, per-lane strips (Video, Audio, Image, Text/Beat, Title), individual clip cards with drag-to-reposition, a ruler showing time markers, clip context menu for actions like split/duplicate/delete, and a transition picker between video clips.
contexts.name: artist-timeline-ui

contexts.description: Media Studio toolbar and beat sidebar. The toolbar exposes composition settings, selected-item property editors (clip trim, title text/font, image scale/position, transition, voiceover), undo/redo, and export trigger. The BeatSidebar lists all TextItem beats keyed to the playback cursor, and the VoiceoverButton initiates TTS generation into the audio lane.
contexts.name: artist-toolbar-beat-sidebar

contexts.description: End-to-end specs for Athena's guided-walkthrough overlay: orb glide, element glow, caption progression, skip/stop controls, and topic-specific walkthrough steps. Covers both the core walkthrough engine and the topic-catalogue smoke (ensuring all registered topics have a defined step sequence).
contexts.name: athena-guided-walkthrough

contexts.description: Repositories for audit incidents — records of policy violations, anomalous behaviors, and security events detected during persona execution. Includes the `audit_incidents_promoter` which classifies and promotes raw execution events into structured incident records for operator review.
contexts.name: audit-incidents-repo

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: login_with_google, get_auth_state, create_external_api_key, approve_pairing, cli_capture_run, detect_authenticated_services
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for user authentication (Google OAuth login/logout, session state), external API key lifecycle (create, list, audit — used by the management HTTP API on port 9420), device pairing approvals (web dashboard ↔ desktop handshakes), CLI credential capture (running service auth flows in a subprocess), and ambient auth detection (discovering which services the user is already authenticated with). These form the identity and access layer.
contexts.name: auth-session-api

contexts.description: Domain types for the automation and event pipeline: `AutomationPipeline` (multi-step automation definitions with deploy status), `PersonaTrigger` / `TriggerConfig` (schedule, webhook, manual, chain trigger variants), `PersonaEvent` (inbound event records with lifecycle), `SharedEvent` (cross-persona event bus payload), and `NotificationSubscription` (user notification preferences per channel).
contexts.name: automation-event-models

contexts.description: Null-rendering background services host (deferred 300 KB of domain store subscriptions past first paint) alongside fleet-facing chrome: the always-on 2 px pulse strip that animates live session activity and opens Fleet Monitor on click, update/CLI-readiness banners, and the pure layout model for the strip's center-out slot algorithm. These components mount once at app root and have no visible DOM beyond their specific zones.
contexts.name: background-fleet-chrome

contexts.description: Staged compilation pipeline framework shared by persona, intent, and workflow compilers. The compilation_pipeline module defines the CompilationPipeline trait and stage machinery; template_v3 bridges the newer v3 template schema (nested use_cases) to the flat AgentIr shape the backend needs; template_checksums manages integrity verification for template manifests.
contexts.name: build-compilation-pipeline

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: start_build_session, stream build events via Channel, promote_build, run_simulation, create_output_assertion, evaluate_assertions
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the Design & Build Studio's build session workflow: streaming build events over a Tauri Channel, managing persisted build sessions, promoting builds, running simulations, and defining output assertions (quality rules evaluated against execution outputs). Build sessions are the iterative compile-and-test loop that turns a design intent into a validated persona.
contexts.name: build-session-api

contexts.description: Multi-turn interactive build session engine that wraps the CLI subprocess in a per-session lifecycle with tokio channels for user Q&A, checkpoint-based SQLite persistence, and real-time Tauri event streaming. The orchestrator fans work out to capability-specific sub-agents, and oneshot mode handles the simple single-capability path without the full multi-turn loop.
contexts.name: build-session-lifecycle

contexts.description: Quality-gating layer inside build sessions: the Rule 16/17 state machine that enforces tool-test and connector-validation gates before promotion, the fix-pass that auto-patches failing steps, the LLM-driven pre-promote test runner, and the system prompt and template-context assemblers that give the build LLM its reference materials. Also includes the stream-JSON parser that translates raw CLI output into typed BuildEvents.
contexts.name: build-session-quality

contexts.description: Repository for Design & Build Studio sessions — tracks the multi-step agent persona construction process where users iteratively configure a persona with Athena's guidance. Build sessions record the conversation state, step progress, and construction artifacts for each persona design session.
contexts.name: build-session-repo

contexts.description: TypeScript types mirroring the Rust build session models for the Design & Build Studio. Defines BuildPhase (lifecycle enum with runtime guard), CellBuildStatus (matrix cell visual state), and the v3 capability-framework domain types (PersonaBehaviorCore, CapabilityDefinition, etc.). Provides isBuildPhase() and isCellBuildStatus() type guards for safe IPC message parsing.
contexts.name: build-session-types

contexts.description: Guided persona build session commands — the step-by-step AI-assisted wizard that collects user answers, infers required tools and connectors, and assembles a persona definition. Includes simulation (dry-run build preview), multi-turn conversations within a session, and review checkpoints.
contexts.name: build-sessions

contexts.description: Auto-generated module containing the static definitions for all built-in connector templates (e.g. GitHub, Slack, Gmail). Generated from JSON source files in `scripts/connectors/builtin/` via `generate-connector-seed.mjs`. Used by `init_db` to upsert connector templates on every app boot.
contexts.name: builtin-connector-seed

contexts.description: P2P bundle packaging (gated behind the p2p feature flag) and one-click share-link server. The bundle module serialises a persona plus its dependencies into a portable archive for peer transfer over the P2P transport. The share-link server generates short-lived, token-authenticated URLs that serve bundle bytes on demand, auto-expiring after 24 hours or first successful download.
contexts.name: bundle-and-sharing

contexts.description: The canonical button set used throughout the app: primary/secondary/ghost/danger/accent Button, AsyncButton (self-disabling spinner wrapper), and CopyButton (clipboard with 'Copied' feedback). Defined once here and imported everywhere; ESLint warns on any hand-rolled alternatives. The CATALOG.md auto-generated index documents all 115+ shared primitives for discoverability.
contexts.name: button-primitives

contexts.api_surface: getByomPolicy, setByomPolicy, deleteByomPolicy, listProviderAuditLog, getProviderUsageStats, getProviderUsageTimeseries, testProviderConnection; getQwenStatus, setQwenCredentials, clearQwenCredentials
contexts.description: Implements the 'Bring Your Own Model' policy layer for enterprise and power users: controls which AI providers (Anthropic Claude, Qwen, etc.) are allowed or blocked, manages per-provider API keys with credential storage, defines task-complexity-based routing rules (simple/complex task → specific provider), enforces workflow-tag compliance rules restricting which providers certain tagged workflows may use, and renders a provider audit log with usage sparklines and timeseries charts. State is managed by useByomSettings which batches IPC calls to the system/byom Rust module.
contexts.name: byom-provider-settings

contexts.description: Capability-centric persona creation view used in the new-persona wizard. Organises capabilities into expandable rows (each with header, summary, and pane tabs for connectors, events, policies, and trigger) and provides a modal for adding new capabilities. The capabilityHelpers utility derives the row data from the raw capability definition.
contexts.name: capability-config-view

contexts.description: Repositories for execution chains (multi-step pipelines linking persona executions in sequence) and BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) configuration. Chains enable complex workflows where one persona's output feeds another; BYOM allows users to configure custom model endpoints beyond the default providers.
contexts.name: chain-byom-repo

contexts.description: Implements SQLite update-hook-based CDC (Change Data Capture) that broadcasts row-level INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE events to an async channel on every pooled connection. The `CdcCustomizer` registers the hook at connection acquisition time; consumers (typically the engine event bus) subscribe via `CdcSender`. Enables real-time reactive UI updates without polling.
contexts.name: change-data-capture

contexts.description: Domain types for human-in-the-loop interaction: `ChatRole` (assistant/user/system with SQLite serialization), `ChatMessage` (conversation history rows), `DeliberationEntry` (structured reasoning steps captured during agent deliberation for review), and `ManualReview` (human approval/rejection records with outcome and rationale). These back the review queue, conversation inspector, and deliberation viewer.
contexts.name: chat-review-models

contexts.description: Drives the Claude CLI process lifecycle: spawning, argument construction, MCP config injection, and capability resolution. The cli_process module manages process I/O streams and timeout; cli_mcp_config generates per-execution MCP server configs from bound connectors; cli_capabilities resolves the effective Claude Code capabilities for a persona execution.
contexts.name: cli-process-driver

contexts.description: Read-only awareness of the user's active interactive Claude CLI session for enriching persona prompts. Discovery finds the running interactive session; transcript reads recent turns from its transcript file; render formats the extracted context for prompt injection; the audit repo persists awareness metadata. Requires dual opt-in (per-persona + global toggle) and a 10-minute freshness gate.
contexts.name: cli-session-awareness

contexts.description: Form UI for connecting and disconnecting from a Personas Cloud orchestrator via URL + API key. Validates URL protocol and hostname client-side before submitting, shows diagnostic output from cloudDiagnose alongside the connect form, and displays the current connected URL when already connected. Used as the 'Connection' tab of CloudDeployPanel.
contexts.name: cloud-connection-form

contexts.description: Root tabbed panel for managing a Personas Cloud orchestrator connection, providing sub-tabs for Connection, Status, OAuth, Deployments, Schedules, and History. Initializes cloud config from keyring on mount, auto-polls the Status tab, switches fetching behaviour per active tab, and mounts useCloudHealthMonitor for automatic reconnection. Exposes a latency badge and a reconnecting ConnectionStatusBadge in the header.
contexts.name: cloud-deploy-panel

contexts.description: Panel for deploying new personas to the cloud orchestrator and managing existing active deployments. Allows selecting a not-yet-deployed persona and an optional monthly budget cap before initiating deploy. Lists active deployments as DeploymentCards with pause/resume/remove actions and inline smoke-test results. Renders ghost card skeletons during cold-fetch states.
contexts.name: cloud-deployments-panel

contexts.description: Implements the polling loop that bridges a cloud execution back to the local Tauri event bus. After a persona is submitted to the cloud orchestrator, this runner polls `GET /api/executions/{id}` at 800ms intervals with exponential backoff, emitting `execution-output`, `execution-status`, `execution-progress`, and `execution-review-request` Tauri events so the frontend streaming hooks work identically regardless of whether the execution ran locally or remotely. A high-water-mark prevents re-emitting lines already seen after an orchestrator restart, and a 7500-poll ceiling (~100 min) caps runaway executions.
contexts.name: cloud-execution-runner

contexts.description: Polls cloud orchestrator connection health every 30 seconds while connected, detects dropped connections, and executes exponential backoff auto-reconnection (5s→10s→20s→60s cap). Uses a generation-counter pattern to safely cancel in-flight async callbacks after unmount or connection state changes without React useEffect race conditions. Stops on auth errors and notifies the user via store error state.
contexts.name: cloud-health-monitor

contexts.description: Displays cloud execution history with filterable list (by persona, status, time period) and aggregated stats cards (total runs, success rate, total cost, average duration). Renders a DailyBreakdownChart for trend visualization, surfaces top error messages from stats, and shows expandable execution rows with full output via an LRU-cached output fetcher. Uses live polling to keep the history current.
contexts.name: cloud-history-panel

contexts.description: Manages OAuth token lifecycle for the cloud orchestrator: initiates the OAuth flow (opening the auth URL in a browser), completes it by submitting the authorization code, refreshes or disconnects existing OAuth tokens. Surfaces current OAuth status (token presence, expiry, scopes) and pending state. Used as the 'OAuth' tab of CloudDeployPanel.
contexts.name: cloud-oauth-panel

contexts.api_surface: GET /health, GET /api/status, POST /api/execute, GET /api/executions/{id}, POST /api/executions/{id}/cancel, POST /api/oauth/authorize, POST /api/oauth/callback, GET /api/oauth/status, POST /api/deployments, GET /api/deployments, DELETE /api/deployments/{id}, GET /api/reviews/pending, POST /api/executions/{id}/reviews/{reviewId}/respond, GET /api/executions/stats, GET /api/personas/{id}/triggers, POST /api/triggers, PUT /api/triggers/{id}, GET /api/shared-events/catalog

All IDs are validated before interpolation into URL paths to prevent path-traversal injection.

Allows adopting (record locally) or undeploying (shut down) each orphan, or dismissing the entire banner.
