contexts.description: Manages cron-style trigger schedules for actively deployed cloud personas. Lists existing triggers per deployed persona, allows toggling enabled state and deleting triggers, shows recent firing history in an expandable row, and provides a create-trigger form with CRON expression input and persona targeting. Ghosts placeholders while the trigger list loads.
contexts.name: cloud-schedules-panel

contexts.description: Displays real-time cloud orchestrator status including worker counts (idle/executing/disconnected), queue depth, active executions, and Claude token availability. Shows an animated execution progress bar for in-progress tasks and a live-poll indicator. Receives data via props from CloudDeployPanel's usePolling cycle and renders framer-motion animated counters.
contexts.name: cloud-status-panel

contexts.description: Cloud persistence layer — Supabase-backed remote sync of local persona data (local-first model, with Rust sync writer). Also covers account-level cloud operations. Provides backup, multi-device access, and the operator cloud subscription surface.
contexts.name: cloud-sync

contexts.description: Cloud webhooks management tab: allows users to register, list, and manage cloud-hosted webhook endpoints that forward events into the Personas event bus. Complements the local smee relay with production-grade external webhook reception.
contexts.name: cloud-webhooks

contexts.description: Cockpit widgets surfacing the decision audit trail and memory graph: decision panels listing Athena's choices with rationale, decision log timelines per conversation turn, linked-decisions and linked-memories graphs for a given execution or message, and a recent-decisions chip strip per persona context. All fetch from the companion decisions and memories APIs.
contexts.name: cockpit-decision-widgets

contexts.description: Cockpit widgets supporting Athena's persona-design and workflow-decomposition flows: model tier choice, observability planning, design capabilities catalog, persona walkthrough plans, persona-ready build summaries, creation offer CTAs, use-case decompositions, trigger-set breakdowns, template match suggestions, browser-test structured reports, and walkthrough offer cards.
contexts.name: cockpit-design-flow-widgets

contexts.description: The 'Explain in Cockpit' widget palette: data-agnostic widgets that Athena populates directly from her reasoning to explain decisions visually rather than as long chat bubbles. Includes verdict cards (recommendation + rationale + caveat), causal flow-step chains, side-by-side comparison cards, chronological timelines, labeled stat grids, and monospace log-excerpt evidence blocks.
contexts.name: cockpit-explainer-widgets

contexts.description: Cockpit widgets covering fleet-level observability and agent status: persona roster overview, connected services health, metric spark KPI tiles, stat grids, execution facts, message summaries, and issue lists. These widgets display live fleet data fetched on mount and are composed by Athena via compose_cockpit for persistent dashboards, or programmatically for contextual overlays.
contexts.name: cockpit-fleet-widgets

contexts.description: The Athena-composed adaptive dashboard panel on the Home Cockpit tab. Fetches a persisted cockpit spec from the backend (composed by Athena via compose_cockpit), falls back to a deterministic default layout when no spec exists yet, and renders each widget in a 12-column grid. Handles contextual overlays, live spec reload on focus and on compose_cockpit Tauri events, and ghost-grid loading choreography.
contexts.name: cockpit-panel

contexts.description: Vitest unit and integration tests for the cockpit widget library. Covers rendering, config-driven content, empty states, and interaction for the most complex widgets (decision log, design capabilities, model tier choice, observability plan, persona ready, persona walkthrough, recent decisions, template suggestions, trigger set, use-case set, and persona stats utility).
contexts.name: cockpit-widget-tests

contexts.description: Global ⌘K command palette that lets users fuzzy-search agents, credentials, templates, automations, and navigation sections from anywhere in the app. Supports agent quick-actions (execute, duplicate, health-check), recent-item tracking, and tier-gated section filtering. Pure utility functions for scoring and item building are tested in isolation.
contexts.name: command-palette

contexts.description: Repositories for the event system — event definitions, shared event catalog subscriptions, event firings, and Smee relay configurations for webhooks. Powers the trigger/automation system by storing the event graph that connects external service events to persona executions.
contexts.name: communication-events-repo

contexts.description: Approval queue and human-in-the-loop action execution — Athena proposes actions (run_persona, resolve_human_review) that land as pending approval rows; the user approves or rejects via UI; approved actions are executed by specialist executors (core, dev, fleet variants). Autopilot mode can auto-approve low-risk actions per configured policy.
contexts.name: companion-approvals

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: companion_init, list_companion_conversations, get_athena_usage_dashboard, bridge_fleet_event, project_tracking_list_subscriptions
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the Athena companion brain plugin: initialization of the disk layout, conversation management, adaptation policy, usage dashboard, browser bridge status, and HMR-safe singleton deduplication. Bridges covers the event-driven side channels that mirror fleet lifecycle, MCP pending requests, and team-assignment outcomes into the companion memory; project tracking manages per-project subscription enabling for the 1h-tick scheduler. Together these form the always-on Athena intelligence layer.
contexts.name: companion-athena-api

contexts.description: Spec verifying the Tauri command surface exposed to the companion plugin: invokeCommand passthrough, backend command round-trips, and message-modal features. Tests backend wiring without requiring a full conversation turn.
contexts.name: companion-backend-commands

contexts.description: Background job worker for long-running Athena tasks (codebase scan, memory curation, connector calls) that run without blocking the chat. Jobs follow a `queued → running → completed|failed` lifecycle, with atomic ownership transfer to prevent double-claim by concurrent workers. On completion a system episode is appended to the chat transcript so Athena's next turn sees the result. Includes orphan recovery on startup, per-job progress reporting via Tauri events, and 30-day retention prune of terminal rows.
contexts.name: companion-background-jobs

contexts.description: Implements the procedural and goal memory tiers. Procedural rules describe durable how-to behaviors Athena follows (e.g. 'lead with stale observability after long breaks') with scope-typed categories (chat/action/memory/build) and carry the same anti-hallucination provenance contract as facts. Goals track user-stated objectives with status (active/paused/completed/abandoned), priority, and an optional target date. The backlog module tracks open action items Athena has committed to, surfaced per-turn so she stays accountable.
contexts.name: companion-behavioral-memory

contexts.description: Core data layer for Athena's (the AI companion's) long-term brain — the graph of semantic facts, procedural rules, goals, rituals, and episodic memories stored as companion nodes and edges. Supports knowledge consolidation workflows where conversation episodes are distilled into durable facts the companion recalls across sessions.
contexts.name: companion-brain-repo

contexts.description: Specs for Athena-driven persona build workflows: real Claude workflow from intent through build, adopt, and promote, and Athena-assisted build via companion chat. Tests the build-session lifecycle end-to-end inside the companion context.
contexts.name: companion-build-workflow

contexts.description: Message rendering components for the Athena chat transcript. Bubble renders individual assistant/user messages with streaming state; ApprovalCard and InlineChatCard surface structured assistant responses; ProactiveCard handles proactive nudges; ConversationSwitcher and BrainViewer provide conversation management and brain knowledge browsing. Drives the chat body layout visible to the user.
contexts.name: companion-chat-bubbles

contexts.api_surface: Tauri events: companion://stream, companion://approvals, companion://proactive, companion://job, companion://guide, companion://recall-preview, companion://turn-summary
contexts.description: Top-level chat panel shell and plugin page for the Athena companion. CompanionPanel is the always-mounted listener host that wires all Tauri backend events (stream, approvals, proactive, recall, job, guide) into the store and coordinates turn lifecycle. CompanionPluginPage renders the tabbed manager surface (Setup/Memory/Voice/Decisions) lazy-loaded by tab.
contexts.name: companion-chat-panel

contexts.description: Message composition surface for chatting with Athena. Composer handles draft text, send logic, slash-command palette, and refine chips. Supporting hooks manage chat scroll position, conversation roster, prompt seeding from external surfaces, and forwarding messages to Athena from other parts of the app.
contexts.name: companion-composer

contexts.description: End-to-end Playwright spec verifying a real 3-message round-trip with Athena (Claude Opus) against the live Tauri app. Tests panel open, conversation reset, message send/await, brain episode count growth, and Memory tab reachability. Per-turn timeout is 5 minutes to accommodate real LLM latency.
contexts.name: companion-conversation

contexts.description: Athena companion core — the primary chat/turn command (streams replies via `companion://stream` Tauri events), conversation history management, and the brain module (episodic memory read/write for Athena's long-term recall). Entry point for all user interactions with the Athena AI companion.
contexts.name: companion-core

contexts.description: Core infrastructure and integration layer for the Athena companion system. Covers disk path resolution (`~/.personas/companion-brain/`), shared utilities (SHA-256, slugify, excerpt, short-id), model routing (which Claude model variant to use per request type), observability/tracing, generated UI anchors for the companion panel, wake-window scheduling, and the top-level companion module declaration. Also includes integration shims connecting Athena to the rest of the app: dev-mode overlay, dev sessions, athena_reaction event handler, connector and plugin adapters, and project context.
contexts.name: companion-core-runtime

contexts.description: Central Zustand store and routing configuration for the Athena companion plugin. Manages all companion UI state including panel open/close, multi-conversation threads, live turn state (streaming text, phase, beat), connector jobs, recall previews, narration timelines, guidance walkthroughs, and the decision layer. Entry point for all other companion contexts.
contexts.name: companion-core-store

contexts.description: Hands-free decision layer that surfaces single numbered-choice prompts above the orb for the user to resolve approvals, human-review items, and incidents without opening the full panel. useDecisionQueue aggregates sources and feeds items one-at-a-time; resolveDecision maps Tauri events to PendingDecision shapes; parseSpokenDecision extracts digit picks from voice input. DecisionsPanel is the manager tab for reviewing design decisions.
contexts.name: companion-decision

contexts.description: Implements the episodic memory tier — an append-only, markdown-on-disk log of every conversation turn and observed agent event. Each episode is written to `~/.personas/companion-brain/episodes/YYYY/MM/DD/` first (source of truth), then indexed into `companion_node` (kind='episode') and `companion_fts` for keyword retrieval. The typed-relation graph module (graph.rs) represents cross-node links (supports/contradicts/derives_from) backed by `companion_edge`, providing a traversal cache over the markdown frontmatter `links:` field.
contexts.name: companion-episodic-memory

contexts.api_surface: Tauri events: fleet session, assignment progress
contexts.description: Integration layer connecting Athena to the Fleet multi-agent orchestration system. useFleetCompanionBridge receives fleet session events and converts them to companion store updates. useCompanionAssignmentBridge and useAthenaAssignmentReconciliation track Athena-dispatched team assignments. CompanionAssignmentCards renders assignment status inline in chat. FleetBoldnessDial and WakeCadence expose fleet-specific controls in the companion.
contexts.name: companion-fleet-bridge

contexts.description: Specs for the Companion ↔ Fleet integration: fleet event recording lands as System brain episodes, Tier-2 dispatcher actions (fleet_send_input approvals) reach the right backend commands, and the orchestration round-trip verifies Athena can drive fleet sessions. Also covers fleet session orchestration end-to-end.
contexts.name: companion-fleet-e2e

contexts.description: Contains Athena's fleet-awareness intelligence layer: pattern recognition over fleet execution history, user decision profiling, profile synthesis for generating insight reports, and recall synthesis for summarizing brain state into a natural-language digest. Also covers the dashboard/cockpit composition ops (compose_dashboard, compose_cockpit, explain_in_cockpit) that let Athena generate personalized observability surfaces and the decisions module that tracks operator decision history for behavioral profiling.
contexts.name: companion-fleet-intelligence

contexts.api_surface: Tauri event: athena://orchestration/digest-changed; MCP tool endpoint
contexts.description: Orchestration layer between Athena and the Fleet (parallel Claude Code workers). Operative memory is an in-process live record of what's happening now (which sessions are running, what Athena dispatched) distinct from brain/ which is the permanent historical record. The MCP module provides tool handlers (report_intent, checkpoint) that fleet workers call back through, plus a pending-approval queue. Fires `athena://orchestration/digest-changed` events so the frontend can pull a fresh live digest without polling.
contexts.name: companion-fleet-orchestration

contexts.description: Athena-driven guided walkthrough system for onboarding users to app features. walkthroughs.ts defines the registry of named step sequences; useGuidanceRunner executes the active walkthrough, advancing steps and writing highlight targets to the store. anchorCatalog maps element test-ids to viewport anchors; appActions lets Athena trigger app navigation as guidance steps; composeAdHoc builds runtime point-at and composed walkthroughs from Athena tool calls.
contexts.name: companion-guidance

contexts.description: Implements the hybrid retrieval layer that bundles memory into a `Recall` struct for each conversation turn. Combines recency (last 5 turns) with vector similarity (vec0 top-K via AllMiniLML6V2Q) across episodes, facts, procedurals, and doctrine. A dedicated kind-scoped doctrine lane prevents episode-heavy corpora from starving doctrine hits. Stable per-turn includes (active goals, top-importance procedurals, open backlog) ensure Athena always sees what she committed to regardless of query phrasing.
contexts.name: companion-hybrid-retrieval

contexts.description: Manages Athena's static constitution and evolving identity profile, plus the doctrine knowledge base (canonical app docs indexed as embeddings). The identity module implements anchored-diff editing (AppendBullet/ReplaceBullet/RemoveBullet ops) gated by approval cards so Athena can propose targeted profile updates without full-file rewrites. Doctrine ingests a curated 22-file allowlist of product docs chunked at H2/H3 boundaries, keyed by `(doc_path, heading_anchor)` for idempotent upserts. Templates provide the embedded constitution and identity markdown scaffolds.
contexts.name: companion-identity-doctrine

contexts.description: Data-shape adapters that normalize diverse backend event types (approval requests, execution outputs, healing events, messages) into the unified inbox item format. Shared utilities provide tone classification and grapheme counting for item rendering. The adapter index exports the full adapter registry consumed by useUnifiedInbox.
contexts.name: companion-inbox-adapters

contexts.description: React hooks that drive the unified Athena inbox experience. useUnifiedInbox aggregates all adapter-normalized items into a single sorted feed. useCockpitSummary derives a dashboard summary for the cockpit view. useIllustration selects an illustration variant for empty-state and loading states. useInboxActions provides action handlers (approve, dismiss, reply).
contexts.name: companion-inbox-hooks

contexts.description: Athena's integration surface — fleet session bridging (Athena monitors and comments on fleet runs), MCP tool bridge (Athena can call MCP tools), plugin dispatching, template suggestions, connector awareness, project tracking context, browser testing assistance, and background job dispatching.
contexts.name: companion-integration

contexts.description: Athena proactive and analytical intelligence — proactive suggestions (Athena self-initiates based on context), sensory input processing (screen/audio awareness), observability feeds to Athena's context, user feedback capture, backlog triage (AI-assisted issue prioritisation), consolidation of memory, and decision-capture (operator corrections logged to the decision ledger).
contexts.name: companion-intelligence

contexts.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool-approval surface inside the companion. mcpRequestStore holds pending MCP tool-use requests that need user approval. McpRequestPanel renders the approval card inline in the chat. useMcpRequestBridge listens for MCP request events from the backend and writes them to the store.
contexts.name: companion-mcp

contexts.description: Implements the memory consolidation and embedding pipeline. Consolidation runs a separate ephemeral Claude CLI call over recent episodes and existing facts to propose semantic-fact updates (`add`/`update`/`contradict`) that land in `companion_consolidation_item` rows for human review. The embeddings module provides vec0 vector storage using AllMiniLML6V2Q (384-dim), with a model-guard that excludes stale embeddings from a swapped model, fuzzy dedup via cosine distance, and importance decay/prune lifecycle management.
contexts.name: companion-memory-pipeline

contexts.description: In-chat progress transparency components that show what Athena is doing during and after a turn. NarrationThread renders live PROGRESS beats and the collapsed post-turn trail; OperationalThread shows the TodoWrite task checklist; ActivityTray surfaces background connector jobs; TurnSummaryChip, RecallStrip, BrainLinksStrip, ConnectorCallCard, and TaskTag provide per-bubble metadata strips.
contexts.name: companion-narration-ops

contexts.description: Athena's floating orb overlay — the minimized companion presence that lives above app content. AthenaOrb handles tap/hold/drag gestures for open, voice-capture, and repositioning. AthenaGuideLayer and TrackedGlowRing provide the element-highlight ring during guided walkthroughs. OrbDecisionBubble surfaces the hands-free decision prompt above the orb.
contexts.name: companion-orb

contexts.description: Operative-memory bridge that keeps Athena's working context visible in the chat. useOperativeMemoryBridge listens to backend operative-memory events and writes them to operativeMemoryStore. parseDigest transforms the raw digest text into structured operation/session records. LiveOpsStrip renders the collapsible ops strip above the chat transcript so power users can see exactly what Athena holds in context.
contexts.name: companion-orchestration

contexts.description: Implements Athena's proactive outreach system — nudges she generates on her own initiative without a user prompt. A 5-stage pipeline: trigger evaluators scan brain state to produce `Nudge` candidates; a quiet-hours guard suppresses delivery during focus/sleep windows; a daily budget cap (default 3) prevents spam; dedup prevents restacking the same trigger; and persistence writes to `companion_proactive_message`. Specialized trigger modules handle execution review, incident alerting, fleet operation wrap-ups, backlog aging, rollup digests, message triage, and scheduled future check-ins.
contexts.name: companion-proactive-messaging

contexts.description: Implements the semantic memory tier: distilled facts about the user, projects, and world. Each fact has three persistence layers — markdown on disk (source of truth), a `companion_node` row (kind='fact'), and a `companion_fact` sidecar with typed metadata (scope, key, confidence, supersedes/contradicts). Enforces an anti-hallucination provenance contract: every fact write must cite ≥1 source episode ID. Also implements touch-last-seen, soft-delete (moves to `_deleted/`), and fact reinforcement for fuzzy dedup.
contexts.name: companion-semantic-memory

contexts.api_surface: Tauri events: companion://turn, companion://token, companion://stream-end; IPC commands via commands/companion/
contexts.description: Manages Athena's multi-conversation chat sessions, spawning and resuming Claude CLI processes per turn via stream-json, parsing events, persisting turns as episodic memories, and dispatching structured ops from assistant replies. Each turn writes episodes to the brain, emits Tauri events for the UI, and supports autonomous continuation sequences up to a hard cap. The dispatcher module extracts JSON proposals from assistant text, validates allowed ops, and creates approval-card rows or fires auto-navigation events.
contexts.name: companion-session-orchestration

contexts.api_surface: Tauri: companion brain, memory consolidation, browser bridge
contexts.description: Companion configuration and memory management panels accessible from the plugin manager tabs. SetupPanel covers Athena's initial configuration including browser bridge connection (BrowserBridgePanel) and sensory signal settings (SensorySignalsModal). MemoryPanel lets users browse and trigger memory consolidation; ConsolidationReview shows the consolidation result for user approval.
contexts.name: companion-setup

contexts.description: Pure parsing and signal-extraction utilities for the Athena CLI stream. Extracts stream phase labels (thinking/tool-use/generating), assistant text deltas, narration timeline entries (PROGRESS beats + tool calls), mid-turn intent signals, TodoWrite operational steps, and brain-links. Also provides audio/chime feedback utilities for turn transitions.
contexts.name: companion-stream-processing

contexts.description: Specs for companion chat panel UI controls: autonomous mode toggle (A2), stop-button presence and click during streaming (A5), design cards rendering, stream-phase indicators (thinking/tool_use/reviewing), autonomous-marker rendering for system messages, and header control states. Uses bridge injection methods to avoid burning real LLM turns.
contexts.name: companion-ui-controls

contexts.description: Voice I/O for the Athena companion — ElevenLabs/Kokoro TTS playback (spoken responses) and real-time speech-to-text input (Whisper-backed STT for hands-free interaction). Pairs with the TTS text field returned by the chat command to enable voice-first companion sessions.
contexts.name: companion-voice

contexts.description: Speech-to-text input pipeline for hands-free interaction with Athena. useSpeechInput and useHoldToTalk implement hold-to-talk capture and transcription dispatch. useDictation and useLocalDictation provide continuous dictation variants. SttPanel exposes the STT engine selector (Web Speech API vs local). VoiceControlPopover surfaces the hold-to-talk control from the footer.
contexts.name: companion-voice-input

contexts.api_surface: Tauri: TTS settings, ElevenLabs API, on-device Kokoro/sherpa-onnx
contexts.description: Text-to-speech output pipeline for Athena's spoken responses. VoicePanel is the settings hub; KokoroVoicePanel and PocketVoicePanel wrap the on-device TTS engines (Kokoro/sherpa-onnx and PocketSphinx). BubbleReadAloud adds per-bubble playback controls. voicePlayback manages audio decoding and blob-URL lifecycle. useTtsSettings and useTtsVoiceSelection manage voice configuration.
contexts.name: companion-voice-output

contexts.description: Text-to-speech engine abstraction for Athena's spoken replies. Ships two local engines: Kokoro (primary, curated high-quality voices via sherpa-onnx sidecar) and Pocket TTS (experimental zero-shot voice cloning). The mod.rs defines shared types (TtsEngineId, TtsSettings, TtsAudio) and validates text/voice-id inputs. Engine-specific modules handle sidecar invocation, catalog management (available voices with metadata), and one-click installer flows that download and extract the model packages to `~/.personas/companion-tts/`.
contexts.name: companion-voice-synthesis

contexts.description: On-device speech-to-text for Athena's voice input using whisper.cpp via a sidecar binary. The mod.rs defines audio validation (WAV format, 16kHz/mono/16-bit PCM, size bounds) and language code validation. The catalog module lists available Whisper models with metadata; the downloader handles model acquisition; and whisper.rs handles sidecar process spawning per transcription call. Only local Whisper paths reach this module — the browser Web Speech Engine is handled entirely in the frontend.
contexts.name: companion-voice-transcription

contexts.description: Type definitions for the multi-agent DAG workflow composition engine. Declares Workflow, WorkflowNode (persona/input/output kinds), WorkflowEdge (data-flow connections), and per-node WorkflowNodeExecution tracking with cost, token, and timing metrics. These types are the shared contract between the workflow canvas UI and the backend execution runner.
contexts.name: composition-workflow-types

contexts.description: Bundles curated API endpoint definitions (5–10 per connector, derived from official OpenAPI specs) that are merged with user-uploaded specs in the API Explorer tab. Provides typed endpoint descriptors with method, path, parameters, request body, and tags, covering connectors like Azure DevOps, GitHub, Linear, and others. Consumed by the API Explorer feature to seed the endpoint catalogue without requiring a live spec upload.
contexts.name: connector-api-endpoints

contexts.description: Automation rules management within the connector tab: create and manage automations that fire when a connector event matches a condition and execute an action. The AutomationSetupModal wizard steps through trigger, condition, action, and review; AutomationCard/CardActions display existing rules with status badges.
contexts.name: connector-automation

contexts.description: Defines the static catalog of builtin connectors (Airtable, GitHub, Notion, etc.) loaded from JSON seeds, plus cross-cutting metadata: functional role groupings (source_control, ci_cd, knowledge_base…), per-connector audience tags (developer/support/manager), and license tier classification (personal/paid/enterprise). Together these power the connector picker's filter, search, and role-interchange UI. Depends on connector JSON seeds under scripts/connectors/builtin/ and i18n types.
contexts.name: connector-catalog-metadata

contexts.description: Unit tests for the builtin connector catalog, verifying that connector definitions loaded from JSON seeds are well-formed and satisfy schema contracts expected by the connector picker and vault UI.
contexts.name: connector-catalog-tests

contexts.description: Connector explorer and readiness assessment commands — browsing available connectors from the catalog, and computing a persona's connector readiness score (are all required credentials bound? are they healthy?). The readiness resolver is used by the build-sessions wizard and persona list views.
contexts.name: connector-design

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_connectors, create_connector, update_connector, discover_connector_resources
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for connector definition CRUD (the schema objects that describe how to authenticate with an external service — field definitions, credential types, healthcheck rules) and connector discovery (dynamically enumerating sub-resources within an authenticated connector, e.g. listing Sentry projects or GitHub repos to populate adoption questionnaire pickers). Connectors are the bridge between credentials and services.
contexts.name: connector-discovery-api

contexts.description: Utility functions for classifying connector types (Google OAuth vs universal OAuth gateway) and extracting OAuth metadata from connector definitions. Prevents scattered instanceof / metadata duck-typing checks across the vault and agent-setup flows from diverging.
contexts.name: connector-helpers

contexts.description: Connector definition lifecycle — creating, discovering, and managing connector schemas that declare how a credential maps to an external service. Includes credential-recipe design (AI-generates a connector schema from an OpenAPI spec or description) and schema proposals.
contexts.name: connector-management

contexts.description: Persona connectors tab showing which external integrations (APIs, tools) are bound to the persona, their readiness status, unfulfilled credential demands, and a verification panel. CredentialPicker lets users bind vault credentials to connector slots. useConnectorStatuses polls connector readiness; useUnfulfilledCredentials derives the gap list.
contexts.name: connector-status

contexts.api_surface: GET contexts, GET context-groups via devTools API
contexts.description: The Context Map feature lets developers visualise and navigate the codebase divided into named, colour-coded context groups. This layer owns the page layout, the ledger table, group-row stats, individual context detail panels, and the group colour picker. It reads contexts and groups from the backend DB and renders them with KPI status overlays.
contexts.name: context-map-core

contexts.api_surface: getScanCodebaseStatus, cancelScanCodebase, listUseCases via devTools API
contexts.description: Runtime layer for the Context Map: manages live codebase scanning state (ScanOverlay), computes KPI health per context, and resolves use-case associations. The useContextRuntime hook drives incremental scan updates via Tauri events; useUseCases fetches and caches use-case rows; UseCaseDetailModal surfaces per-use-case drill-down. Tests cover the runtime hook and the Coverage view.
contexts.name: context-map-runtime

contexts.description: Context map generation and export pipeline — runs incremental scans over managed project source trees to discover contexts (business features), groups them, audits coverage, and exports both a machine-readable `context-map.json` and an annotated CLAUDE.md block into the managed project root. Also covers use-case and static analysis scans.
contexts.name: context-scanning

contexts.description: Provides AES-256-GCM symmetric encryption and RSA session-key pair generation for securing credentials over the IPC bridge, a conservative secret-redaction pass that scrubs high-confidence credential patterns and high-entropy tokens from stored execution traces, and the ring-buffer healthcheck ledger primitives for tracking per-credential liveness over the last 20 checks.
contexts.name: core-crypto-redact

contexts.description: Defines the app-wide `AppError` enum that every fallible function returns, and the unified `ErrorCategory` / `ErrorTaxonomy` that all subsystems (healing, failover, design drift, frontend) share for error classification. Centralising taxonomy here eliminates the four independent heuristic copies that previously diverged across `healing`, `personaSlice`, `designDrift`, and `healthCheckSlice`.
contexts.name: core-error-handling

contexts.description: The foundational type definitions and singletons that every other crate in the Personas desktop build depends on. Provides the execution state machine via the `declare_lifecycle!` macro, engine kind enum, hard execution ceilings, the SQLite connection-pool type alias, the IPC in-flight counter, event name constants, and the managed drive root cache. These primitives cannot depend on any other Personas crate — they sit at the very bottom of the dependency graph.
contexts.name: core-foundation-types

contexts.api_surface: Shared HTTP clients: SHARED_HTTP, SSRF_SAFE_HTTP, INTERNAL_HTTP
contexts.description: Provides the process-wide shared `reqwest` HTTP client singletons and an SSRF-safe DNS resolver that rejects private/internal IP addresses at connection time. The `SsrfSafeDnsResolver` closes the DNS-rebinding window (CWE-367) by re-validating every redirect hop, ensuring outbound requests from user-supplied credential URLs cannot reach loopback or RFC-1918 ranges.
contexts.name: core-http-safety

contexts.description: The foundational model infrastructure: the `models` module root that re-exports every domain type, the `DbSchema` struct describing database table metadata, the `Json<T>` newtype for SQLite JSON columns, and `serde_util` helpers (e.g. `double_option`) used by dozens of models to handle nullable-update payloads correctly.
contexts.name: core-model-primitives

contexts.description: Central type hub that bridges ts-rs Rust bindings to the shapes React components consume. Declares enriched persona aggregates (PersonaWithDetails), the CredentialMetadata/ConnectorDefinition hierarchy with parse helpers, navigation union types (SidebarSection, EditorTab, OverviewTab, and 15+ other tab enums), and cross-cutting enrichment utilities such as enrichWithPersona(). Nearly every feature module imports from here.
contexts.name: core-persona-types

contexts.description: Pure, feature-gate-neutral retrieval primitives extracted from the companion brain: hybrid per-kind lane ranking, vector-distance relevance floor filtering, and excerpt-vs-full-body decision logic. No DB pool, disk, or async dependencies — inputs are scored `(id, distance)` tuples. Enables persona-memory injection and companion retrieval to share a single verified implementation without an `ml` feature dependency.
contexts.name: core-retrieval

contexts.description: Small shared utilities used across every layer of the codebase: a `now_ms()` epoch clock needed by both the Fleet registry and the data layer without creating a cross-layer dependency, char-boundary-safe string truncation helpers, and a secret/email sanitization pass that masks API keys and PII before they reach audit logs or error paths.
contexts.name: core-utilities

contexts.description: Input validation for the Tauri IPC boundary: HTML/XSS stripping via ammonia, persona field constraints (name length, system prompt size, timeout clamping against engine limits), trigger schedule and webhook validation, chat message validation, memory content checks, and build-session contract verification. All validations return `AppError::Validation` so the frontend receives structured error messages.
contexts.name: core-validation

contexts.description: Intercepts unhandled frontend errors, sanitizes stack traces and stack-frame arguments to strip credentials and file paths, then persists the crash report to localStorage and reports it to the backend for Sentry ingestion. Ensures crash diagnostics are useful without leaking sensitive runtime data.
contexts.name: crash-persistence

contexts.description: The manual authoring modal for adding a new knowledge item to a workspace library. Collects kind, title, statement, topic (slash-path taxonomy), optional origin project, and optional markdown evidence detail. Submits as `proposed` status with human provenance via createWorkspaceKnowledge.
contexts.name: create-practice-modal

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: artist_get_blender_status, artist_start_session, artist_execute_render_plan, radio_list_stations, radio_play, radio_get_state
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the Artist plugin (Blender MCP integration: session management, 3D render plan pipeline, composition loading, asset library) and the Radio plugin (SomaFM stream player: station listing, play/pause/stop/skip, now-playing metadata, radio state). These are the creative and ambient media plugins that run alongside agent work.
contexts.name: creative-media-api

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: start_google_credential_oauth, start_auto_cred_browser, start_credential_design, get_credential_recipe, upsert_credential_recipe
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the multiple pathways to acquire and populate credentials: OAuth gateway flows (Google, generic providers), automated browser-based credential capture (Chromium subprocess, 11-min timeout), AI-guided credential design, and credential recipe caching (connector → field prefill recipes ranked by usage). Together these minimize friction in getting a credential from zero to healthcheck-passing.
contexts.name: credential-acquisition-api

contexts.description: Authentication and credential acquisition flows — OAuth browser flow, CLI token capture, automatic credential detection from running processes, desktop keychain bridge, foraging (scanning local configs for existing keys), and negotiator (interactive step-by-step credential setup). These commands bring credentials in from the environment.
contexts.name: credential-auth

contexts.description: Domain types for the entire credential and connector surface: `Credential`, `LedgerHealthEntry` (ring buffer row), `CredentialRecipe` (parameterised rotation recipe), `ConnectorDefinition` (capability contract), `ExternalApiKey`, `OAuthTokenMetric`, and `RotationPolicy`. These are the canonical structs shared between the security commands, the vault UI, and the rotation engine.
contexts.name: credential-connector-models

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_credentials, create_credential, update_credential, healthcheck_credential, get_vault_status, list_rotation_policies
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the core credential store: CRUD for persona credentials (AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest), bulk and per-credential healthchecks against live services, vault status and migration, and credential rotation policy management (scheduled key rotation, anomaly scoring, OAuth token lifecycle metrics). This is the authoritative read/write surface for the encrypted vault.
contexts.name: credential-core-api

contexts.description: Hooks for the credential negotiation sub-flow within persona design: orchestrating a step graph of credential requirements, querying which credentials are available (foraging), applying a design result's credential bindings, and driving the negotiator UX through required/optional credential steps. Bridges the design analysis output to the Security & Credentials domain.
contexts.name: credential-design-hooks

contexts.description: Provides credential field classification logic — determining which fields are sensitive vs. non-sensitive, canonical field key names, and key-rename mappings. Used by credential repositories, migration helpers, and data-portability commands to consistently classify and normalize credential data across the app.
contexts.name: credential-fields

contexts.description: AI-assisted credential intelligence commands — natural-language vault queries, debug helpers, API proxy (relays requests through stored credentials), AI artifact flow for credential generation, external API key management, and OpenAPI autopilot (reads a spec and auto-configures credential requirements).
contexts.name: credential-intelligence

contexts.description: Parses the JSON `metadata` field stored on a credential row into a typed `CredentialLedger` — a structured record of healthcheck history, OAuth token lifecycle state (expiry, refresh count, backoff), anomaly score, and usage metrics. Provides a safe parser that returns a well-typed default when the stored JSON is null or invalid. Consumed by any UI or logic that needs to read credential health state from the database.
contexts.name: credential-ledger-parsing

contexts.description: Credential lifecycle management: windowed-anomaly healthchecks with sliding 5m/1h/24h failure-rate windows, OAuth token proactive refresh before expiry with per-refresh observability metrics, credential rotation policies, and the connector-strategy registry that consolidates healthcheck, rotation, and token-refresh logic into one extension point per connector type.
contexts.name: credential-lifecycle

contexts.description: Design-time credential modeling and runtime negotiation between personas and their required connectors. The credential_design module defines the credential schema and UI hint types for the design surface; credential_negotiator resolves which credentials are available, missing, or need re-auth before execution starts, and surfaces structured gap reports to the frontend.
contexts.name: credential-negotiation

contexts.description: Maintains an in-memory + IPC-backed cache of credential recipes — the discovered OAuth/field/healthcheck schemas for each connector. When the Design flow discovers a connector's credential shape, it saves a recipe so that subsequent Negotiator or AutoCred sessions can skip AI discovery and reuse the cached result. Acts as a shared registry across all credential setup flows within a session.
contexts.name: credential-recipe-registry

contexts.description: Implements an event-driven remediation pipeline for credential anomalies. The bus receives `RemediationEvent` signals from healthchecks and anomaly scoring, deduplicates within a cooldown window, and dispatches to the executor which carries out auto-rotation, auto-disable, or OS notification actions. Provides an observable action log for UI feedback and uses idempotent IPC calls to the vault's rotation API.
contexts.name: credential-remediation

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_gateway_members, add_gateway_member, list_connector_resources, set_scoped_resources, sign_document, verify_document
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for credential resource scoping (pinning a credential to a subset of its available sub-resources, e.g. a GitHub PAT limited to two repos), MCP gateway membership management (bundling multiple MCP-speaking credentials under one gateway attachment point for persona tool routing), and cryptographic document signing (peer-to-peer document signature creation and verification). These are advanced credential access-control primitives.
contexts.name: credential-scoping-api

contexts.description: Repository for vault credentials — encrypted storage of API keys, OAuth tokens, and service authentication data. Manages AES-256-GCM encrypted credential blobs, IV storage, and credential metadata. Serves as the secure backing store for the Connector Catalog and Vault features.
contexts.name: credentials-repo

contexts.description: Core scheduling primitives: a 5-field cron expression parser using O(1) bitmask matching, timezone-aware schedule validation helpers, a performance digest configuration struct validated by the settings layer, the `EvolutionCycleStatus` state machine for genome breeding runs, and harvest scope territory definitions that partition the codebase into bounded agent-readable segments for the practice-harvest engine.
contexts.name: cron-scheduling

contexts.description: Encrypted cross-device persona continuity layer providing content hashing, a three-way merge algorithm, and snapshot serialization. The workspace_sync module holds the pure data model and conflict resolution (last-writer-wins with device-id tiebreak); the crypto submodule handles AES-GCM snapshot encryption; merge implements the three-way diff algorithm; worktree_settings manages per-worktree execution configuration.
contexts.name: cross-device-workspace-sync

contexts.description: Manages front-end side of hybrid IPC encryption for secure credential passing to the Rust backend. Caches the backend's session public key with staleness detection — on rotation (vault re-key, panic recovery) the stale key is detected within ~60 seconds and re-imported without a reload. Used whenever sensitive data must cross the IPC boundary encrypted.
contexts.name: crypto-utils

contexts.description: Hooks for managing shared in-memory data collections: a persona-id-to-name map, a module subscription pattern for plugin-style data streams, persisted context across navigation, filtered and layered list views for large datasets, and background snapshots for diffing. These primitives are consumed widely by feature modules to avoid duplicating data-wrangling logic.
contexts.name: data-collection-hooks

contexts.api_surface: getExportStats, exportFull, exportSelective, importPortabilityBundle, exportCredentials, importCredentials; storageUsage, pruneStorage
contexts.description: Enables workspace portability: shows a live inventory of the user's data (personas, teams, tools, credentials, memories, test suites, KPIs), supports full or selective export to an encrypted bundle file, bundle import with conflict resolution, a separate passphrase-protected credential vault export and import flow, and local SQLite storage usage reporting with a safe-prune tool for old execution records. State is managed by useDataPortability which orchestrates IPC calls to the system/dataPortability and system/system Rust command modules.
contexts.name: data-portability-settings

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: start_nl_query, get_nl_query_snapshot, get_db_schema, start_schema_proposal
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the Database Explorer feature: natural-language-to-SQL query execution (streaming job results with generated SQL and explanation), database schema inspection (table/column/index metadata from a connected credential), and AI schema proposal generation (suggesting schema improvements or new tables). These commands require a live database credential and power the in-app SQL workbench.
contexts.name: database-explorer-api

contexts.description: Hooks for the in-app SQL database explorer feature: introspecting the live SQLite schema, splitting raw SQL text into executable statements, proposing schema changes from natural language, and surfacing query debug information. Enables the Database Explorer panel where users can inspect and query the agent's working database.
contexts.name: database-explorer-hooks

contexts.description: Implements the pre-migration safety snapshot policy: copies the existing `personas.db` to `<data_dir>/backups/` before any migration chain runs, then rotates old snapshots so only the three newest backup sets are kept. Skips fresh installs (no existing DB to protect). Each backup set includes WAL/SHM sidecars.
contexts.name: db-backup

contexts.description: Handles additive schema evolution after the initial baseline — ALTER TABLE column additions, new index creation, new table creation for features added post-baseline, and the composite trigger fires table. Each statement is idempotent (guarded against duplicate-column errors). Also owns FK hygiene utilities and credential field migration helpers.
contexts.name: db-migrations-incremental

contexts.description: Contains the canonical initial SQL schema DDL for all core application tables, created as a consolidated idempotent migration from the original 11 versioned Vibeman migrations. This is the single source of truth for the database structure at baseline — all subsequent changes go through incremental migrations. Consumed by `migrations::run()` at every app boot.
contexts.name: db-migrations-schema

contexts.description: Manages the SQLite connection pool lifecycle, WAL/pragma configuration, and database initialization sequence. Handles fresh installs and upgrade-on-boot paths including migration execution, FTS backfill, builtin data seeding, and orphan-row cleanup. Exposes `init_db`, `open_pool_at`, `init_user_db`, and `seed_builtin_credentials` as the main entry points consumed by the Tauri app setup.
contexts.name: db-pool-init

contexts.description: Provides reusable query-builder helpers, shared macros for CRUD code generation, and row-mapper utilities that reduce boilerplate across all repository modules. Also includes performance measurement helpers for tracking query latency. These primitives are the foundation for the entire repository layer.
contexts.name: db-query-utilities

contexts.description: Dead-letter queue viewer for failed/undeliverable events. Shows events that could not be processed so operators can inspect, retry, or discard them. Part of the event-bus reliability surface.
contexts.name: dead-letter

contexts.description: Shared decision-stream UI components used across review, backlog, and knowledge surfaces: DecisionActions (accept/reject controls), DecisionRow (list row with title, supporting line, facts, and verdict chip), and the shared TypeScript decision model types. Callers supply the data; these components supply the uniform visual language for acting on AI-generated decisions.
contexts.name: decision-review

contexts.description: Top-level unified deployment dashboard that aggregates Personas Cloud and GitLab agent deployments into a single sortable, filterable table view. Fetches deployments from both targets on mount, merges them into UnifiedDeployment rows, computes summary stats (active/paused/cloud/gitlab counts, total invocations), and orchestrates search/filter/sort state alongside bulk selection. Delegates table rendering to DeploymentTable, filters to DeploymentFilters, and health sparklines to useDeploymentHealth.
contexts.name: deployment-dashboard

contexts.description: Monitors deployment health by fetching CloudExecutionStats for each unique personaId in the deployment list and mapping daily breakdown data back to individual deployment row IDs for sparkline display. Uses a stable-key optimization to avoid re-fetching when persona IDs haven't changed, and maintains a stats cache to prevent unnecessary API calls on re-mapping. Skips GitLab deployments (no personaId) automatically.
contexts.name: deployment-health

contexts.description: Sortable, selectable data table rendering UnifiedDeployment rows with actions (pause, resume, undeploy, test, open URL). Renders per-row health sparklines from healthMap, inline smoke-test results with pass/fail badges, and a ghost-row skeleton during cold-fetch states. Implements a one-shot entrance cascade (35ms stagger, id-guarded to prevent replay on poll) following the docs/design/overview-loading.md pattern.
contexts.name: deployment-table

contexts.description: Manages one-click smoke-test execution for individual deployed personas. Calls executePersona with a standard smoke-test prompt, tracks running/pass/fail state per deployment ID, surfaces cost and duration inline, and auto-dismisses results after 15 seconds. Cleans up all pending timers on unmount to prevent stale setState calls in React 19.
contexts.name: deployment-test

contexts.description: Defines the shared type system for the unified deployment dashboard, merging Personas Cloud and GitLab agent deployments into a single normalized model. Provides DeployStatus, DeployTarget, UnifiedDeployment interfaces plus status-mapping functions (mapCloudStatus, mapGitlabStatus) that normalize heterogeneous backend tokens into a consistent lifecycle vocabulary. Also exposes sort helpers (compareValues) and badge-styling utilities consumed by all other deployment UI components.
contexts.name: deployment-types-core

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: start_design_analysis, refine_design, start_adopt_template, get_adopt_snapshot, transform_n8n_workflow, rate_template, list_team_presets, list_platform_definitions, list_recipes
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the AI-assisted persona design pipeline (start/refine/cancel design analysis, feasibility testing, compile-from-intent), template adoption (snapshot polling, answer submission for AI-guided questionnaire), n8n workflow import-and-transform (converting n8n workflow JSON into persona drafts), template rating/feedback, localized team presets, and platform definition management (custom node-type schemas for non-standard automation platforms). Together these power the full persona creation funnel from template or blank canvas.
contexts.name: design-template-api

contexts.description: JavaScript-side design token registry for spacing, motion durations, color helpers, and status/severity palettes. Used alongside Tailwind CSS classes to guarantee consistent visual rhythm across all components. Also provides colorWithAlpha for programmatic hex-to-rgba conversion used in chart and overlay renderers.
contexts.name: design-tokens

contexts.description: Typed action bridges to native desktop applications (VS Code, Terminal, Finder, etc.) executed via CLI, local API, or filesystem. The bridge_manifest module manages per-app manifest discovery; desktop_discovery scans for installed apps; desktop_runtime hosts the bridge execution sandbox; desktop_bridges provides the concrete per-app action implementations gated by the security approval system.
contexts.name: desktop-app-bridges

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: dev_tools_list_projects, dev_tools_list_kpis, dev_tools_create_kpi, dev_tools_list_milestones, dev_tools_list_use_cases, dev_tools_get_autopilot_mode, dev_tools_list_workspaces, dev_tools_workspace_harvest
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the full Factory & Projects feature: dev project CRUD and directory scanning, skill installation, goals with signals and dependency graphs, ideas, context groups, tasks, competition tracking, and strategy stats (devTools.ts); KPI definitions, measurements, and bindings (kpis.ts); ship-layer milestones with use-case membership and bucket classification (milestones.ts); use-case slice definitions and status lifecycle (useCases.ts); per-project autopilot mode control (autopilot.ts); and the workspace knowledge center — cross-project practice libraries, harvest, ingest, and adoption matrices (workspaces.ts). This is the entire Factory cockpit IPC surface.
contexts.name: dev-projects-kpi-api

contexts.description: Developer Tools feature backend — the main dev_tools command file (projects, ideas, tasks, pipelines, KPIs), a standalone HTTP bridge for CI/external tooling, and multi-workspace management. Powers the Dev Tools feature that lets operators track projects and backlog inside Personas.
contexts.name: dev-tools-core

contexts.description: Sub-feature modules for Developer Tools — competition tracking, context management, git operations, goal management, milestone tracking, portfolio views, triage rules, and workspace management. Each module is a focused slice of the Dev Tools product surface, reusing the shared dev_tools repo.
contexts.name: dev-tools-features

contexts.description: Repositories for Athena's Developer Tools plugin — dev memories (long-term learnings about codebases), dev run checkpoints (state between multi-step CLI sessions), and the dev tools backlog (capability gaps and self-promises Athena tracks). Enables Athena to maintain context across multiple autonomous development sessions.
contexts.name: dev-tools-repo

contexts.description: Top-level shell for the Dev Tools plugin — routes between all sub-modules via a tab key from the system store. Hosts the page header, the shared project dropdown, and constant catalogs (idea categories, colors, badges, preset skills, scan agents) consumed across every sub-module. Acts as the single lazy-import boundary for all dev-tools pages.
contexts.name: dev-tools-shell

contexts.description: The Director meta-persona that coaches every other persona by reading its shape, recent behaviour, and open issues, then emitting prose verdicts into the Human Review layer. Users approve/reject verdicts which are captured back as director_feedback memories. Extends into the Obsidian Brain for long-term note persistence, and includes a memory-dedup/archive pass that keeps the persona's recall context lean. The deliberation module provides a pure state machine for moderator-governed multi-turn design deliberations.
contexts.name: director-coaching

contexts.description: Small but frequently used display utilities: Collapse (pure-CSS animated expand/collapse container), InlineEditableText (click-to-edit inline field), connectorRunnability (pure logic for connector runnable/configured checks), and FieldHint (inline hint text showing valid range or examples beneath a form field). These fill gaps not covered by the larger display sub-categories.
contexts.name: display-collapse-inline

contexts.description: Read-only display primitives for time and numeric data: RelativeTime (live 'Xh ago', absolute on hover), AbsoluteTime (fixed date/time/datetime with relative hover), Numeric (canonical locale/precision/unit number renderer), UuidLabel, Tooltip (hover/focus), TruncateWithTooltip (overflow text + full value tooltip), and SectionLabel (uppercase section heading). These are the blessed alternatives to ad-hoc .toLocaleString() or title= calls.
contexts.name: display-data-formatters

contexts.description: Animated metric display components for KPI and analytics surfaces: StatCard (icon chip + label + big value + trend delta), AnimatedCounter (number animates old→new), SpringCount (spring-physics count-up), ConfidenceArc (semi-circular gauge), AnimatedList (staggered-delay list), RevealItem (single-row progressive reveal), and RechartsWrapper (code-split lazy chunk loader for recharts to avoid child-identity issues).
contexts.name: display-metrics-counters

contexts.description: Motion presets and empty-state illustration components used across the app: MotionizedGlyph (multi-path SVG self-drawing with centre-out reveal), motionPresets (shared Framer Motion preset definitions — draw, stagger, fade-pop, float, pulse, hover-response, success-settle), EmptyIllustration, IllustratedEmptyState, ChartEmptyState, HeroMesh (decorative noise background), DensityToggle, and DesignConnectorGrid.
contexts.name: display-motion-empty

contexts.description: Visual vocabulary for expressing status, activity, and classification at a glance: StatusBadge (token → label + colour via tokenLabel()), StatusDot, StatusShape, ActivityDot (emerald/amber/muted), LiveStatusDot (with ping halo), Badge (generic tag pill), BusinessOutcomeBadge, CategoryChip, and ActivityPulseIcon (animated pulse for the title-bar process tray). All use semantic design tokens; none hard-code colours.
contexts.name: display-status-badges

contexts.description: Full suite of table and list layout primitives: UnifiedTable (standard sortable table), SortableHeader (clickable column with sort indicator), ColumnResize (drag handle), DataGrid (CSS-grid fraction layout), DragHandle (grip icon), DropIndicator (DnD position indicator), ScrollShadowContainer (overflow fade), FacetedDecisionTable (slash-path facet tree + toolbar + grid), GroupedVirtualList (virtualized sticky-header grouped list), and their pure model/grouping logic and tests.
contexts.name: display-table-primitives

contexts.description: Multi-tab editor for reviewing and modifying an n8n-derived persona draft before it is committed. Provides Prompt, Settings, and JSON tabs that let operators tune the AI system prompt, persona metadata, and raw JSON payload. Accepts an N8nPersonaDraft shape and exposes update callbacks consumed by the n8n wizard's confirm step.
contexts.name: draft-editor

contexts.description: Core file-browser UI components: toolbar (path bar, new folder/file, view switcher), folder tree sidebar with recent-files rail, file/folder list with multi-view modes (list/icons/columns), kind-filter bar, and trash banner. These components compose the primary Finder-style browsing surface of the Drive plugin and receive all state from useDrive via props.
contexts.name: drive-browser-components

contexts.description: Secondary UI layer for the Drive plugin: details pane showing selected-entry metadata, right-click context menu with all file actions, image/video/PDF lightbox for in-app preview, empty-state hint, confirmation prompt dialog, and the drop-count chip widget used in drag-over affordances. These overlay and panel components receive the drive state and action callbacks from DrivePage.
contexts.name: drive-detail-components

contexts.description: Knowledge-base ingestion bridge that connects the Drive file sandbox to the vector KB feature (available only in the ML-enabled desktop-full build). useDriveKnowledge feature-detects KB availability at runtime, translates drive-relative paths to absolute filesystem paths, and dispatches background ingest jobs (files via kb_ingest_files, folders via kb_ingest_directory). KbPickerDialog lets users choose or create a target knowledge base, and DriveKnowledgeDrawer provides a read surface over the chosen KB. DESIGN.md documents the feature's availability model.
contexts.name: drive-knowledge

contexts.api_surface: Tauri: drive_list, drive_list_tree, drive_mkdir, drive_rename, drive_delete, drive_move, drive_copy, drive_search, drive_storage_info, drive_recent, drive_write_text
contexts.description: Master state hook for the Drive Finder UI that owns navigation history, entry list, selection model, clipboard (copy/cut/paste), sort/filter/view preferences, storage info, recent-files rail, per-folder scroll memory, and all file mutations (create, rename, delete, move). Persists view-mode and sort preferences to localStorage across sessions. Implements a concurrency-capped bulk-operation runner to parallelise multi-file IPC calls without saturating the Tauri IPC thread.
contexts.name: drive-navigation-state

contexts.description: OCR text-extraction sub-feature for the Drive plugin. useOcr detects whether a Google Gemini credential is connected in the vault and exposes its ID so the backend wrapper can decrypt and use the API key server-side without exposing it to the frontend. DriveOcrDrawer renders the extraction UI, shows results, and can write the extracted text back to a new drive file.
contexts.name: drive-ocr

contexts.description: Root page component for the Drive plugin, wiring together all sub-features (navigation, selection, drag-drop, signing, OCR, knowledge) into a single orchestrated view. Also owns the file-type visual design system (icon presets, colour tokens, kind weights, trash name parsing, and relative-time formatting) shared across every Drive view. Entry point for the Drive sidebar route.
contexts.name: drive-page

contexts.description: Smoke test for the Drive plugin (Google Drive / cloud storage integration): verifies the plugin renders in the expected state and basic UI interactions work against the live app.
contexts.name: drive-plugin-e2e

contexts.api_surface: Tauri: sign_document, verify_document, generate_signing_key, list_document_signatures, delete_document_signature, export_signature_sidecar
contexts.description: Document signing and verification sub-feature within the Drive plugin. useSigning bridges the P2P signing backend (sign_document, verify_document) with the drive-relative path world, manages the user's signing identity (auto-generates an Ed25519 key pair on first use), and maintains an in-memory history of signed files for badge display. DriveSignDialog, DriveVerifyDialog, and DriveSignaturesPanel provide the sign/verify/history UI surfaces.
contexts.name: drive-signing

contexts.description: Unit and component test suite for the Drive plugin. Covers designToken utilities (visual preset resolution, kind bucket ordering), component rendering for DriveEmptyHint and DropCountChip, the useDrive state hook (navigation, selection, mutations, search), and useScrollShadows behaviour. Also includes integration-level tests for image blob preview rendering.
contexts.name: drive-tests

contexts.description: Reusable low-level hooks that support the Drive UI. useScrollShadows tracks whether a scroll container has content above or below the visible viewport (top/bottom fade affordance) using ResizeObserver. useLazyImageThumb uses IntersectionObserver to load image bytes via Tauri IPC only when a tile is near the viewport, and revokes the blob URL when it scrolls away to bound memory on large image folders.
contexts.name: drive-utility-hooks

contexts.description: Shared rich-content editor and preview components: JsonEditor (JSON editing with validation), MarkdownRenderer (sanitized markdown to React), PromptTabsPreview (tabbed preview of prompt variants), and PromptTemplateRenderer (renders prompt templates with highlighted {{variable}} placeholder syntax). Used wherever the app lets users view or edit structured content.
contexts.name: editor-components

contexts.description: Displays and lets operators toggle a capability matrix showing which CLI operations (persona execution, design analysis, credential health check, n8n transform, test generation, healing analysis, recipe execution, query debug, etc.) each installed AI provider supports. Also exposes a per-operation model routing section for fine-grained control over which model handles each task category. Capability overrides are serialised to the engine_capabilities key in app_settings via the system API.
contexts.name: engine-capability-matrix

contexts.description: Engine module root and cross-cutting infrastructure: the mod.rs re-export hub that surfaces personas_core and personas_engine crates; AI helper utilities for LLM output extraction; LLM topology prompt builder for multi-persona workflow composition; system-operation runtime (context_scan); management HTTP API (/api/*) for external tool control; recipe seed bootstrap; dynamic resource discovery for adoption questionnaires; background job framework for user-persona curation jobs; and the leadership module that coordinates which process instance owns singleton background loops.
contexts.name: engine-core-infrastructure

contexts.description: Cross-cutting engine utilities shared across all engine modules. The str_utils module provides string manipulation helpers; config_merge resolves per-execution configuration by merging persona-level and workspace-level settings (ConfigSource enum); persona_icon normalizes custom-icon: scheme values for safe serialization across export boundaries.
contexts.name: engine-shared-utilities

contexts.description: Error handling infrastructure: Sentry integration, the error registry that maps raw errors to i18n-friendly messages, toastCatch/silentCatch helpers, and frontend crash reporting to the Rust backend.
contexts.name: error-analytics

contexts.description: Evaluation run management — structured evaluation batches that assess persona output quality against expected criteria, plus execution audit-incident logging (unexpected behaviours, policy violations), annotations on execution records, and clipboard intelligence (tracking what content personas generate). Used by operators to run quality gates.
contexts.name: eval-runs

contexts.description: Core event and notification infrastructure — the event registry (all named events personas can emit/subscribe to), shared event types used across modules, notifications (push delivery to the user), and SLA tracking (per-persona reliability targets). This is the real-time signal backbone for the observability layer.
contexts.name: event-bus

contexts.description: Typed event bus that routes persona events to subscribers and drives trigger-based execution. The bus module implements event matching against subscriptions and PersonaTrigger rows; the event_registry wraps Tauri's emit API with typed payloads; event_vocabulary and shared_event_local_relay handle event naming and local relay bridging.
contexts.name: event-bus-routing

contexts.description: Reactive subscription framework that powers all background polling and event-driven automation. The ReactiveSubscription trait captures the source→predicate→action pattern; composite triggers evaluate AND/OR/sequence conditions with time windows against the event log; the polling loop fans out to per-persona pollers on each tick.
contexts.name: event-subscriptions

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: shared_events_browse_catalog, list_notification_subscriptions, list_system_op_automations, list_recipes
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the shared event feed (cross-service event catalog subscriptions that flow into persona triggers), notification subscription management (push channels for execution outcomes), system-op automations (binding built-in backend operations like context scans to schedules or events), and the persona recipe library (reusable capability building blocks). These wires together the reactive automation layer.
contexts.name: events-automation-api

contexts.api_surface: list_executions, get_execution, start_execution, stop_execution, schedule_persona, get_ambient_status
contexts.description: Primary execution command surface — listing, inspecting, and triggering persona runs. The scheduler command layer exposes cron-style scheduling controls; ambient mode handles background always-on execution. Reads from the executions DB repo and cross-references the automation runner and circuit-breaker.
contexts.name: execution-core

contexts.description: Deep-dive execution detail view presenting a waterfall trace inspector, subagent tree, tool-call cards, cost breakdown bar, span rows, log viewer, memory viewer, summary card, and chain-trace view for chained persona runs. ErrorExplanationCard surfaces Athena-generated explanations for failed executions. The TraceInspector is the primary entry point.
contexts.name: execution-detail-inspector

contexts.description: Two algorithmic primitives for the evaluation layer: `ScoreWeights` — the single source of truth for composite lab score weights (tool accuracy, output quality, protocol compliance) seeded to the frontend at startup via `lab_get_score_weights` — and `TopologyGraph` — a unified Kahn's topological sort with cycle detection that replaced three independent copies across the team, topology, and optimizer modules.
contexts.name: execution-evaluation

contexts.description: Self-healing and evolutionary adaptation of persona executions — detects failure patterns, triggers recovery strategies, evolves genome-level configuration, and enforces policy events (rate limits, budget gates). These commands form the reliability and adaptation loop around the core runner.
contexts.name: execution-healing

contexts.description: Extracts structured intelligence from completed executions and upserts it into the execution_knowledge table, creating a knowledge graph that improves future runs. Includes the shared KB search that embeds a query and searches every knowledge base for best matches (the single implementation consumed by both clipboard-intelligence and subscription paths), and the memory-reflection engine that consolidates related memories into higher-level insights to prevent recall budget bloat.
contexts.name: execution-knowledge

contexts.description: Lab, testing, and knowledge-management commands for persona execution experiments — prompt-variant experiments, assertion suites, test-suite management, and the persona knowledge base (retrieved context injected at execution time). Enables iterative prompt engineering and quality gating.
contexts.name: execution-lab

contexts.description: Paginated execution history list with filtering, bulk rerun, cost sparklines, and a side-by-side comparison view for two selected executions. The ExecutionList drives useExecutionList for data fetching; ComparisonTable/Diff/Metrics delegate to a Web Worker for heavy diff computation; BulkRerun manages multi-select requeue flows.
contexts.name: execution-list

contexts.description: Repositories for execution performance metrics snapshots, LLM spend tracking, and run budget enforcement. Captures aggregated statistics (latency, cost, token consumption) at multiple granularities for the observability dashboard and KPI tracking features.
contexts.name: execution-metrics-repo

contexts.description: A compact always-visible execution mini-player shown outside the editor for ongoing runs. ExecutionMiniPlayer displays the current step and status with a pipeline-dot progress strip (PipelineDots), enabling users to monitor execution progress from any part of the app without navigating to the full runner view.
contexts.name: execution-mini-player

contexts.description: Observability-oriented hooks that watch a running execution for file system changes, system-level traces, AI self-healing stream events, reasoning traces, and timeline replay. Enables the activity monitor panel and the post-execution replay surface to reflect what the agent did during its run.
contexts.name: execution-monitoring-hooks

contexts.description: Defines the 7-stage typed execution pipeline (initiate → validate → create_record → spawn_engine → stream_output → finalize_status → frontend_complete) with a unified span-based trace model shared between frontend pipeline stages and backend engine spans. Manages the terminal output ring buffer with byte-budget enforcement and throttled store flushing, the canonical execution state machine (queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled), and a parallel SystemTraceSession mechanism for tracing non-execution system operations (credential design, template adoption, etc.) using the same UnifiedSpan shape.
contexts.name: execution-pipeline-core

contexts.api_surface: getKnowledgeInjection API call; Sentry captureMessage; storeBus execution:completed event
contexts.description: Implements and registers all pipeline middleware that run at specific stage boundaries: knowledge-graph guidance injection (validate stage), audit logging (create_record + finalize_status), Sentry telemetry capture (finalize_status), stage-timing persistence to localStorage (frontend_complete), storeBus notification emission (frontend_complete), budget-cache invalidation (frontend_complete), and design-drift detection comparing execution outcomes against persona design expectations (frontend_complete). The central index.ts wires all middleware in priority order at app startup.
contexts.name: execution-pipeline-middleware

contexts.description: Priority-based queue and concurrency management layer that controls how many personas execute simultaneously. Implements per-persona queue depth limits, global concurrency caps, rate limiting, session pooling, and a pre-prepared run cache for fast startup. Ensures fair scheduling across concurrent executions.
contexts.name: execution-queue-scheduler

contexts.description: Time-scrubbing replay sandbox for reviewing a past execution as if it were happening live. Provides transport controls (play/pause/seek), a pipeline waterfall, terminal replay panel, tool panel, cost accrual overlay, and a cost replay panel. The ReplaySandbox orchestrates replay state via useReplayState.
contexts.name: execution-replay

contexts.description: Core repository for persona execution records — stores every run of a persona (status, token usage, cost, duration, tool calls, output), supports full-text search via FTS5, and provides the query surface for the executions dashboard and observability features. The most frequently read table in the system.
contexts.name: execution-repo

contexts.description: Resilience layer for persona execution: provider failover with circuit-breaker pattern, incident auto-continuation (resumes blocked executions after an incident is resolved), resource-aware admission control based on CPU/memory load, and integration tests for circuit-breaker behaviour. Together these ensure the engine degrades gracefully under provider failures or host stress.
contexts.name: execution-resilience

contexts.description: Domain types for the execution data layer: `Execution` (the persisted run record), `ExecutionAnnotation` (user/agent tags on individual runs), and `SystemOp` (background maintenance operations). These structs are the canonical DB row shapes consumed by the execution repository and surfaced to the frontend via Tauri IPC.
contexts.name: execution-state-models

contexts.description: Core hooks for consuming live execution output from the Tauri backend as it streams. Handles persona-owned output filtering, correlated CLI stream pairing, structured stream parsing with typed handlers, execution scope detection, and per-execution summary aggregation. The primary integration point between the Tauri execution engine IPC and React UI components such as ChatTab and PersonaRunner.
contexts.name: execution-streaming-hooks

contexts.description: Records execution cost, token usage, and process-level activity signals for observability. The cost module tracks per-execution token and dollar spend; logger writes structured execution logs; process_activity monitors active process signals for the desktop overlay and health dashboards.
contexts.name: execution-telemetry

contexts.description: Low-level execution trace primitives: stage bar and sub-span bar for rendering timeline stages, SyntheticTrace for constructing synthetic trace trees from raw events, stage colour mapping, the chain-trace hook, and shared lifecycle UI icons. Also includes the Web Worker that performs heavy diff computation for execution comparison.
contexts.name: execution-trace-primitives

contexts.description: Two complementary execution-cost primitives: `trace.rs` implements a span-tree execution tracer that records root → child spans (prompt assembly, credential resolution, CLI spawn, tool calls) with timing and token attribution, storing traces as JSON in `execution_traces`; `run_budget.rs` provides a run-level cost ceiling across multi-spawn operations (evolution cycles, lab matrices) where `--max-budget-usd` per-spawn is insufficient.
contexts.name: execution-tracing-budget

contexts.description: A prototype UI harness for granular selective export: a scope rail for choosing export categories (personas, teams, credentials, KPIs, etc.), a scrollable manifest cart showing selected items with counts, atom/panel/row primitives for the picker layout, and a useExportPicker hook that fetches live data from personas, credentials, teams, and KPI APIs to populate the selection UI. This is an experimental refinement of the ExportSelectionModal, kept isolated in the export-prototype sub-directory while it matures.
contexts.name: export-picker-prototype

contexts.description: Repositories for external service integrations — MCP gateway configurations for Model Context Protocol servers, n8n session tracking for workflow automation, owned device registry, Playwright procedure definitions for browser automation, and OCR job records.
contexts.name: external-integrations-repo

contexts.api_surface: runWorkspaceMiners, runWorkspaceDivergence, prepareWorkspaceHarvest, listHarvestCoverage, ingestWorkspaceHarvest, verifyWorkspaceAdoptions
contexts.description: The dropdown menu for extracting practices from workspace member repos.
