contexts.description: Repositories for human review workflows — manual review requests triggered when personas encounter uncertainty, chat review sessions for interactive oversight, and template feedback collection. Enables human-in-the-loop patterns where executions can pause for human approval before proceeding.
contexts.name: review-feedback-repo

contexts.description: The Run Desk is the execution surface for dispatched dev tasks — a paged, event-driven task queue replacing the old Task Runner. It renders tasks grouped by status, supports retry/cancel, shows real streaming output via TaskOutputPanel, manages auto-run banners backed by dev_auto_runs, and surfaces a self-healing panel that recommends retries for failed tasks. PrBridge handles PR integration.
contexts.name: run-desk

contexts.api_surface: pub(crate) async fn resolve_credential_env_vars, inject_connector_credentials, inject_credential, force_refresh_credentials_for_tool
contexts.description: Resolves which connector credentials a persona's tools need, decrypts them from the vault, refreshes OAuth tokens on demand, and injects every field as a prefixed environment variable into the spawned CLI process. Implements a three-tier fallback strategy (service-match → name-match → direct service_type) plus a design-context second pass so generic tools like `http_request` can still reach connector secrets. Guards against credential-driven env-var hijacking of the child process.
contexts.name: runner-credential-injection

contexts.api_surface: pub(crate) fn sanitize_env_name, pub(super) fn credential_refresh_lock
contexts.description: Provides the env-var name sanitizer (`sanitize_env_name`) that guards the child CLI subprocess against credential-driven injection attacks, blocking exact dangerous names (PATH, LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, etc.) and runner-config prefix families (NPM_CONFIG_, UV_, BUN_, etc.). Also owns the per-credential OAuth refresh mutex pool that prevents concurrent executions from racing on the same grant.
contexts.name: runner-env-sanitization

contexts.description: Applies global app settings (Ollama base URL, LiteLLM master key, Qwen endpoint, etc.) onto a per-persona `ModelProfile` when the persona hasn't overridden those fields, implementing the workspace/global cascade for provider configuration. Also provides the canonical zero-valued `ExecutionResult` struct used by early-abort paths throughout the orchestrator.
contexts.name: runner-global-settings

contexts.description: The top-level pipeline that runs a persona: spawns the Claude CLI as a subprocess, streams its output through four labelled stages (Validate → SpawnEngine → StreamOutput → FinalizeStatus), and persists results. It coordinates every other runner helper — credential injection, prompt assembly, memory injection, sidecar installation, BYOM policy, and provider failover — before and after the subprocess live.
contexts.name: runner-orchestrator

contexts.api_surface: pub fn build_team_alignment_block(pool, persona, team_name, team_id) -> Option<String>
contexts.description: Builds the team-alignment block injected into every team-member persona's prompt: who the teammates are and what they own, the team's active goals with advancing markers, open high/critical incidents to avoid repeating, user channel directives, and the project's branching/standards policy. Keeps the injected block cost-bounded via hard caps on roster size, goal count, and incident count.
contexts.name: runner-team-context

contexts.description: Calendar visualisation of scheduled agent fires in week and month layouts. Future fires are projected via cron_fire_times_in_range IPC (seeded with trigger id for H-spread accuracy); past cron slots are matched against real execution records within a 90s tolerance window so colour coding reflects actual outcomes rather than fabricated health. Detects and highlights scheduling conflicts within 5-minute windows.
contexts.name: schedule-calendar-view

contexts.api_surface: executePersona, updateTrigger, backfillSchedule, previewCronSchedule, cronFireTimesInRange, listTriggers
contexts.description: Per-schedule row UI and the action hook that drives all schedule mutations: manual execute, toggle enabled, change frequency (cron/interval/timezone), skip next fire, delayed run (run-in-N-minutes), and user-initiated backfill. Uses read-modify-write on trigger config to preserve active_window and rate_limit settings. Exposes a conflict-preview hook that debounces cron_fire_times_in_range IPC calls.
contexts.name: schedule-row-actions

contexts.description: Inline run-history surfaces attached to schedule rows: a per-trigger history panel with a 14-day sparkline showing success/failure trends and a link to the execution detail modal, plus a global recent-runs section at the top of the timeline showing the last 24 hours of scheduled fires across all agents. Both auto-refresh and respect the active group filter.
contexts.name: schedule-run-history

contexts.description: Unit tests for the schedule feature's pure-logic helpers: slot-to-run matching (matchPastSlotsToRuns, classifyRunOutcome), calendar event orchestration (useCalendarEvents), and schedule list flattening (flattenScheduleGroups, scheduleListItems). Tests verify correctness of the tolerance-window binding algorithm and the grouped/windowed list collapse.
contexts.name: schedule-tests

contexts.api_surface: getSchedulerStatus, startScheduler, stopScheduler, listScheduleMissedRuns, clearScheduleMissedRuns, fetchCronAgents
contexts.description: Main schedule management page that lists all cron-triggered agents grouped by time window (overdue, next 15 min, next hour, etc.). Polls the backend every 30 seconds and coalesces refresh calls via in-flight deduplication. Provides scheduler engine start/stop, group filtering via sidebar custom events, and switches between grouped and calendar views.
contexts.name: schedule-timeline

contexts.description: Canonical schedule/cron type definitions and normalizers. The Schedule interface (cron expression, interval_seconds, IANA timezone) is the single source of truth for trigger scheduling, unifying three previously divergent frontend shapes. Includes toSchedule() for converting CronAgent DTOs and fromScheduleConfig() for back-compat with legacy trigger config forms.
contexts.name: schedule-types

contexts.description: Canonical cron preset list and day-of-week vocabulary shared across all scheduling UIs (agent use-cases, trigger configuration, schedule pickers). Consolidates three previously divergent copies with conflicting Mon=0 vs Mon=1 conventions. The triggerConstants module extends this with trigger-type icons, colors, and category taxonomy.
contexts.name: scheduling-primitives

contexts.description: Guided 5-step wizard modal for creating and editing scraper configurations. Steps cover Source (URLs + name), Extract (field rules via LLM builder or manual), Preview (dry-run), Output (dataset + key field), and Schedule (cron + enabled toggle). Form state is managed by `useScrapeForm`, which serialises to/from the wire `ScraperConfigInput` format; step completion is tracked for the progress rail.
contexts.name: scrape-editor-wizard

contexts.api_surface: listScraperConfigs, listScraperDatasets, saveScraperConfig, runScraperConfig, deleteScraperConfig, queryScraperDataset, previewScraperExtract (via @/api/scraper)
contexts.description: The primary monitoring surface for web scraper configurations. Renders a dense operations table (Control Room variant) showing all scrapes with their sources, extracted fields, schedule, last run time, and status, topped by an at-a-glance stat bar. Backed by `useScraperData`, which manages CRUD operations and a module-level cache to avoid cold-load flicker on return visits.
contexts.name: scraper-control-room

contexts.description: Repositories for security audit logging — tracks credential access, API key usage patterns, settings changes, and rotation schedules. Provides the audit trail operators need for compliance review and detecting unauthorized access patterns.
contexts.name: security-audit-repo

contexts.description: Masks sensitive values in JSON payloads and error messages before they are rendered in the UI or sent to Sentry. Redacts keys matching patterns like password, token, api_key, and connection_string, and strips file paths, IP addresses, and internal hostnames from error text. Used by crash persistence, error display, and cloud review flows.
contexts.name: sensitive-data-masking

contexts.description: Sensor and media-capture integrations — OCR (optical character recognition of screen content), radio/audio stream capture, and Google Drive file access. These three thin command wrappers bring external data sources into the persona execution pipeline.
contexts.name: sensor-capture

contexts.description: Surfaces two meta-settings views: an immutable audit log of all settings changes across every sub-module (filterable by category, paginated at 100 entries, with collapsible before/after value diffs), and an internal developer reset panel that clears the first-use consent modal via a two-step confirm. Both views are administrative in nature and do not hold user-facing preferences. The audit log reads from settings_audit_log via the listSettingsAuditEntries API.
contexts.name: settings-audit-admin

contexts.description: Provides the top-level settings page orchestrator that lazy-loads and idle-unmounts each settings tab, the ambient context toggle panel, inline appearance pickers for the chrome bar, the command-palette search integration that deep-links to every settings sub-section, and two shared cross-cutting utilities (two-step confirm hook and recent-change audit chip). Acts as the routing and composition layer that binds all settings sub-modules together without owning domain logic itself. Depends on the settings audit log API for the RecentChangeChip badge.
contexts.name: settings-shell

contexts.description: Shared / marketplace event feed catalog (Watchtower): displays curated external event feeds (e.g. API update notifications), lets users subscribe/watch individual feeds, and shows recent change-activity per feed with a history modal. Backed by useSharedEvents and useSubscribedFeeds hooks.
contexts.name: shared-event-feeds

contexts.description: Hooks for the application sidebar shell: badge counts for unread items, live agent activity indicators, codebase-linked persona discovery, a what's-new indicator for release notes, and breadcrumb trail generation for deep navigation paths. These hooks keep the persistent chrome layer in sync with app state without coupling feature modules to the sidebar directly.
contexts.name: sidebar-chrome-hooks

contexts.description: Two-level collapsible sidebar with icon rail (L1) and label-level nav (L2), section badges, tier gates, and group nav. Persists collapsed state in localStorage and adapts for mobile. Section-specific sub-navs for Agents, Plugins, and Teams inject domain content into the L2 slot, while BadgeSlot and OrbitDots supply unread-count and active-item decoration.
contexts.name: sidebar-navigation

contexts.description: Spec verifying sidebar navigation across all main sections of the app: checks that each SidebarSection renders correctly, navigation state updates, and no regressions in routing between sections.
contexts.name: sidebar-navigation-e2e

contexts.description: Core building blocks of the 8-petal sigil visual language: the root public API index, the canonical GlyphDimension/GlyphRow/GlyphPresence type system, CapabilitySigil (single-capability sigil with empty variant), InteractiveSigil (clickable/hoverable canvas wrapper), SigilPetal (individual SVG petal element), SigilLegend (dimension key), SVG pattern definitions for petal fill styles, layout helper math (stackOffset), dimensional metadata (DIM_META, PETAL_ANGLES), and the aura/glow art layer.
contexts.name: sigil-core

contexts.description: Skill file management and usage tracking — reads Claude Code skill definitions from disk, exposes them for in-app display, and records skill invocation telemetry. Powers the skill browser in the Dev Tools UI and provides the data for skill-usage analytics.
contexts.name: skill-management

contexts.api_surface: getSkillCoverage, getSkillUsage, runStaticScan via devTools API
contexts.description: Analytics sub-tab of the Skills Manager showing coverage pipelines, skill scoreboards, usage history tables, and static scan configuration. useSkillsAnalytics derives coverage metrics from context × skill matrices; StaticScanCard and StaticScanConfigModal orchestrate background code-quality scan runs against the active project's contexts.
contexts.name: skills-analytics

contexts.description: Writes per-connector SKILL.md files and hooks_sidecar configs into the execution directory so Claude Code's native skill/hook discovery picks them up lazily, shrinking the system prompt. The skills_sidecar writes per-connector skill files; hooks_sidecar writes per-execution hook configs; skill_scratchpad provides a per-execution scratch space; connector_explorer generates structured connector documentation for design-time exploration.
contexts.name: skills-hooks-sidecar

contexts.api_surface: installSystemSkill, listSkills, adoptSkill, shareSkill via devTools API
contexts.description: The Skills Manager shows the workspace-global skill library alongside the active project's installed skills, enabling adopt, share, and dispatch operations. skillsManagerData fetches workspace passport data and resolves install/usage/coverage state; SkillsManagerBoard renders the dual-panel exchange UI; UseSkillDialog lets operators dispatch a skill with context and target (Fleet or clipboard).
contexts.name: skills-manager-core

contexts.description: Smee.io webhook relay tab: configures and monitors a local smee relay channel that proxies external webhooks to the local desktop app for development or testing. Includes a switch to jump to the live stream after firing a test webhook.
contexts.name: smee-relay

contexts.description: Provides spend governance and concurrency control for persona execution: operators set a monthly USD cost ceiling that blocks further executions once crossed, and configure the maximum number of parallel persona executions (1–20). Displays a 5-month trailing spend bar chart sourced from the observability metrics API to contextualise the ceiling choice. Persists both limits as typed keys in app_settings via the system/settings IPC bridge.
contexts.name: spend-limits

contexts.description: Instruments Zustand store async actions with the browser Performance Timeline API (performance.mark / performance.measure). Wraps any async store action so its latency appears in DevTools and can be correlated with rendering. Errors still emit their end-mark so partial timing data is preserved.
contexts.name: store-performance

contexts.api_surface: previewPrompt(personaId, sp?): Promise<string> — calls preview_prompt Tauri command
contexts.description: Single source of truth for the StructuredPrompt data model used by the persona editor — types, creation, migration from flat strings, parsing, validation, serialization, markdown rendering, and editable-draft conversion. The module bridges local rendering and the Tauri preview_prompt IPC call, falling back gracefully when the IPC is unavailable. Section summary and diff helpers support the prompt lab version viewer.
contexts.name: structured-prompt

contexts.description: Per-project build configuration controls surfaced in a popover off the chat input: effort level (fast/balanced/deep/max), Athena voice/style (concise/balanced/teaching), enabled MCP connectors (Docs, Browser), and global design knobs (spacing, corner radius, type scale, vibe) that send templated nudge prompts to Athena. All settings write to the active project's runtime slice in studioStore so every subsequent turn picks them up without the user re-specifying them.
contexts.name: studio-build-controls

contexts.description: The conversational interface for steering Athena during a build: a collapsible dock (StudioChatInput) docked bottom-centre over the live preview, a streaming message log with a typewriter reveal (StudioMessages), a first-class decision card that lets Athena surface a numbered-choice question and the user answer by click or keypress (StudioDecision), and context-aware quick-action chips derived from the live build plan (StudioQuickActions). Together they form the turn-based dialogue that drives the build without covering the preview.
contexts.name: studio-chat

contexts.description: Business logic for committing Studio draft routes to live trigger bindings. studioCommit.ts encodes the commit flow (signal-source vs form-commit vs direct commit), studioDraftModel manages the in-memory draft state, and studioLabels/studioCommit constants provide display strings and type guards. Includes unit tests.
contexts.name: studio-commit-logic

contexts.api_surface: webbuildScaffold, webbuildDevStart, webbuildDevStop, webbuildSessionSend, webbuildSessionStop, webbuildStatus, webbuildListProjects, webbuildListRoutes, webbuildNextReady, webbuildRegisterExisting
contexts.description: The runtime backbone of the Athena web-dev Studio: a persistent Zustand store that keeps each project's build state alive across tab switches and app navigation, a localStorage-backed history store that restores display state after WebView reloads, a typed build-phase model with progress helpers, and the top-level StudioPage shell that wires projects, previews, and tab state together. The store subscribes to Tauri companion-stream events and drives all IPC calls (scaffold, start, send turn, stop) so builds continue even when the user is elsewhere in the app.
contexts.name: studio-core

contexts.description: Visualisation of the Athena build plan as a right-edge sliding drawer (StudioPlanDrawer) containing a vertical timeline stepper (StudioChecklistStepper) where each phase node fills as work progresses. The drawer sits beside the preview rather than over the chat so the user can read the plan while steering. The animated PlanGlyph SVG (a traced, self-drawing checklist timeline art) provides the decorative header glyph, with path data auto-generated by the motionize skill and normalised to four semantic colour roles for dark/light theme compatibility.
contexts.name: studio-plan

contexts.description: Multi-project lifecycle management: a browser-style tab strip (StudioTabBar) showing live status dots per open project with a picker for new/import/re-open, a vision-phase onboarding screen (StudioVisionStart) with prompt starters that seed the initial Athena build session, a version history panel (StudioVersions) that lists build-turn git snapshots and restores them safely, and a global attention pill (StudioAttention) that surfaces across the app when Athena is waiting for a decision in a Studio project the user isn't currently viewing.
contexts.name: studio-project-management

contexts.description: State management and helpers for the Studio's live routing inventory. useRoutingState computes EventRow + Connection data from raw triggers and events, and exposes mutation handlers for add-persona, disconnect, and rename-event operations. buildEventRows and routingHelpers provide the derivation logic.
contexts.name: studio-routing-state

contexts.description: System-event automation panel inside the Chain Studio: lets users wire built-in system events (startup, focus-change, etc.) to persona executions without manual trigger setup. SystemEventAutomationsPanel lists active automations; useSystemOpStudio provides the data layer; SystemEventCommitModal handles creation.
contexts.name: studio-system-ops

contexts.api_surface: Supabase PostgREST: POST /rest/v1/{table} (upsert), GET /rest/v1/{table}?..., PATCH /rest/v1/{table}?..., DELETE /rest/v1/{table}?...
contexts.description: Incremental desktop-to-cloud sync writer that periodically (45s tick + event-driven dirty wakes) pushes secret-free projections of 11 local SQLite tables to the user's Supabase tenant via PostgREST upserts. `sync/mod.rs` orchestrates pass lifecycle, fault-isolated per-table syncing, tombstone-based delete propagation, and in-memory status snapshots; `sync/client.rs` is a thin PostgREST HTTP client (upsert/GET/PATCH/DELETE with 500-row chunking); `sync/cursor.rs` persists per-table RFC3339 watermarks + a stable device ID in `app_settings`; `sync/rows.rs` defines the secret-scrubbed row projections and the SQL that reads changed rows since each table's cursor, including AES-GCM payload decryption + secret-redaction for event payloads.
contexts.name: supabase-sync-pipeline

contexts.description: Slice managing ambient contextual awareness — tracking the currently active workspace context, file focus, and session-level signals that Athena and other intelligence features consume for proactive suggestions and context-aware responses.
contexts.name: system-ambient-context-state

contexts.description: Slices for external platform integrations at the system level — cloud provider settings, GitLab repository connections, and deployment target configuration. These slices bridge the app to CI/CD pipelines and cloud hosting environments.
contexts.name: system-cloud-integration-state

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_app_setting, bulk_get_settings, get_tier_usage, get_export_stats, portability_import, get_byom_policy, update_byom_policy
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for global app configuration: key-value app settings (bulk read/write with audit log), tier usage snapshots and rate bucket consumption, data portability (export stats, competitive import previews, credential import), BYOM (bring-your-own-model) policy management (provider routing rules, compliance rules, audit entries, usage timeseries), and the shared string-literal enum unions that keep IPC payloads type-safe across the frontend.
contexts.name: system-config-api

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: system_health_check, health_check_local, get_crash_logs, get_system_metrics; HTTP GET http://127.0.0.1:9420 (management API)
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for system diagnostics: cascading per-section health checks with a structured report, crash log retrieval (both Rust panics and frontend errors), DB performance snapshots, log directory stats, and a memoizing management API auth helper (fetches the system Bearer token for localhost:9420 once and caches it). Also includes real-time CPU and memory sampling for the status-bar load gauge.
contexts.name: system-core-api

contexts.description: Slices powering the developer tools overlay — code context scanning, project indexing, task management, triage workflows, and the dev-tools scanner that maps file contexts. These slices back the DevInspector and context-scanning features used during active development sessions.
contexts.name: system-devtools-state

contexts.description: System health monitoring, MCP integration status, storage metrics, crash telemetry, and binary dependency detection (probing for FFmpeg, whisper, etc.). Provides the diagnostic layer that the app's health dashboard reads to surface capability gaps and system-level issues.
contexts.name: system-health

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_gitlab_config, deploy_to_gitlab, get_cloud_status, cloud_oauth_authorize, discover_desktop_apps, import_mcp_servers, execute_api_request, get_ambient_context_snapshot
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for optional platform integrations: GitLab (config, users, projects, deploy pipelines, rollback, persona versioning), Qwen remote LLM engine (credentials, status, model config), cloud deployment (config, OAuth, deployments, executions, triggers, Smee relays), desktop app discovery (scanning for installed apps and importable MCP servers), API proxy (forwarding authenticated requests to credential-bound endpoints), and ambient context (screen/sensor policy, snapshot, rule matching). These wires in the cloud and third-party layers.
contexts.name: system-integrations-api

contexts.description: Slices managing new-user onboarding flow, guided product tour steps, and initial workspace setup. The onboarding slice tracks completed steps and wizard progress; tourSlice manages spotlight anchors and step sequencing; setupSlice tracks first-launch configuration.
contexts.name: system-onboarding-state

contexts.description: Top-level Zustand stores for cross-cutting app concerns: the system store composes UI, cloud, GitLab, onboarding, tour, dev-tools, fleet, network, and plugin slices. Satellite stores handle i18n locale selection, command palette state, toast notifications, and remote command dispatch.
contexts.name: system-store-root

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: cloud_sync_status, cloud_sync_now, remote_command_list_pending, remote_command_approve, fetch_roadmap
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for desktop-to-cloud data sync, remote command approval, and the live roadmap feed. Cloud sync pushes execution and metric snapshots to a Supabase dashboard mirror (enabled/disabled, manual trigger, status polling). Remote commands are web-dashboard-originated run requests awaiting desktop approval. The live roadmap fetches a remotely-hosted JSON changelog with ETag caching and a bundled fallback.
contexts.name: system-sync-api

contexts.description: Slices and stores controlling application UI state — panel visibility, active sidebar section, modal open/close state, view mode flags, and theme selection (dark/light/system). The themeStore persists the chosen theme and applies it via CSS data-theme attributes.
contexts.name: system-ui-theme-state

contexts.description: Provides safe wrappers around Tauri IPC command invocation. Includes detection of unregistered backend commands and retry classification via ApiError, preventing misleading not-found errors from masking real business logic failures. Depends on tauriInvoke and the TauriErrorKind type system.
contexts.name: tauri-ipc-utils

contexts.description: Tracks real-time progress of team assignments by subscribing to TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_PROGRESS Tauri events. Applies incremental assignment-step updates to the pipeline store and dispatches toast notifications for assignment state transitions. Includes both per-team and global (cross-team) listener variants.
contexts.name: team-assignment-tracking

contexts.description: Pipeline control panel, toolbar, optimizer, and debug tooling for the legacy team DAG canvas. The debugger supports dry-run step-through with variable inspection; the assistant provides a conversational interface for canvas edits; the optimizer analyses the pipeline for bottlenecks. All sit above the canvas core reducers.
contexts.name: team-canvas-controls

contexts.description: Core state and graph model for the legacy DAG team pipeline canvas (now orphaned by the Studio redesign). Manages the canvas reducer, derived canvas state, drag context, team graph topology calculations, and shared constants such as connection-type styles and persona avatar rendering. These files underpin the node/edge layers above them.
contexts.name: team-canvas-core

contexts.description: Visual node and edge components for the legacy team pipeline DAG canvas. Persona nodes display agent avatars with role badges and context menus; edge components render typed connections (sequential, conditional, parallel, feedback) with legends, ghost previews for in-progress wiring, and delete tooltips. Alignment guides assist with layout snapping.
contexts.name: team-canvas-nodes-edges

contexts.description: Manages real-time team communication channels including a channel detail modal and a singleton channel service that subscribes to TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_PROGRESS events and runs a polling fallback. Renders channel payloads and messages via collabRender. Previously each surface had its own listener per team; this centralises refresh to avoid N×M subscription costs.
contexts.name: team-collaboration-channels

contexts.description: Domain types for the team collaboration layer: `Team` (org-level grouping), `TeamAssignment` (persona membership in a team), `TeamChannel` (communication channel configuration), `TeamMemory` (shared knowledge accessible to all team personas), and `TeamPreset` (reusable team configuration templates). These types back the collaborative multi-persona workflow features.
contexts.name: team-collaboration-models

contexts.description: Inter-team communication layer — team channels for message exchange between personas, shared team memories for persistent cross-persona context, and deliberation commands for structured decision-making within a team. Enables asynchronous coordination between grouped agents.
contexts.name: team-communication

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_team_channel, create_team_deliberation, list_team_memories, get_team_memory_stats
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the team communication channel (a keyset-paginated feed of step events, memories, messages, and deliberation turns), team deliberations (structured multi-agent debate sessions with cost budgets and agenda items), and team memories (cross-run knowledge accumulated by teams). Together these form the shared cognitive layer for multi-agent teams.
contexts.name: team-communication-api

contexts.api_surface: createTeamDeliberation, advanceTeamDeliberation, approveDeliberationAction, resolveDeliberationEscalation, splitTeamDeliberation, mergeDeliberationTracks
contexts.description: Implements an autonomous multi-agent deliberation system where a team moderates a topic through structured rounds of discussion. Supports parallel tracks, capability gating (approve/skip), escalation resolution, cost budgeting, and a run-to-budget loop. Polls the active deliberation at 6s intervals so the UI reflects autonomous moderator progress in near-real-time.
contexts.name: team-deliberations

contexts.description: Shared type definitions for team configuration, design review workflows, and persona templates. teamConfigTypes.ts covers team goal structures and workspace settings; designTypes.ts defines the DesignReview lifecycle and scoring model; templateTypes.ts declares the template schema consumed by the Build Studio's template picker and recipe system.
contexts.name: team-design-template-types

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_teams, create_team, create_team_assignment, resolve_step_review, list_assignment_templates
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for persona team CRUD and team assignment orchestration. Teams group personas into a multi-agent workforce with topology blueprints and pipeline analytics; assignments are the top-level orchestration unit that decomposes a task into steps, dispatches them to team members, and manages step reviews and outcomes. Drives the Team Studio and pipeline orchestration UI.
contexts.name: team-management-api

contexts.description: Provides a shared knowledge store for teams — a paginated CRUD panel for team memories with category/search/run filters, importance ratings, timeline view, and run-diff summaries. The hook useTeamMemories orchestrates IPC calls against the team memories API and exposes filter, load-more, and CRUD handlers to panel components.
contexts.name: team-memory

contexts.description: Orchestrates team assignments from DAG walking through step-level status transitions (pending→matching→running→done/failed/skipped/awaiting_review) to terminal outcome, with parallel step execution up to the concurrency cap. The matching layer provides three strategies (manual, LLM-suggested, skill-based) to assign a step to a persona+use_case pair. The preset-adopter turns filesystem-shipped TeamPreset manifests into live PersonaTeams with persona adoption and connection wiring.
contexts.name: team-orchestration

contexts.description: Handles the in-app preset adoption flow where users browse, preview, and adopt pre-built team configurations. The gallery showcases themed presets (web-development, SDLC, backlog-execution, etc.) and the studio renders a connection graph and process blueprint before adoption. Driven by pipelineStore.presetFlowOpen.
contexts.name: team-preset-studio

contexts.description: Implements the split-pane team studio where users configure a selected team's roster, capability toggles, and assignment console. Includes publish controls for exporting teams as presets and a replay view for past assignments. Replaced the old React Flow DAG canvas as the primary team authoring surface.
contexts.name: team-studio

contexts.description: Compiles natural-language workflow descriptions into deployable multi-persona team topologies and wires the connection graph into runtime event chains. The workflow_compiler translates prose into a TeamBlueprint and persists the PersonaTeam + member/connection rows; team_handoff derives chain triggers and event listeners from connection edges; team_preset_loader reads JSON manifests for the presets gallery; topology types and heuristics support canvas rendering and analytics.
contexts.name: team-topology

contexts.description: Provides the top-level team selection and workspace entry point. Renders a team list when no team is selected, and hands off to TeamStudioSplitVariant when a team is chosen. Also hosts the auto-team modal and blueprint preview for team composition.
contexts.name: team-workspace-shell

contexts.description: Repositories for team collaboration features — team definitions, team memory shared across personas, team channel configurations, notification subscriptions, and team-to-persona assignments for orchestration. Enables multi-agent coordination under shared team contexts.
contexts.name: teams-collaboration-repo

contexts.description: Team entity management — creating, listing, and managing teams of personas; assigning personas to teams; and team-level metadata. Provides the organisational unit that groups personas for coordinated multi-agent work.
contexts.name: teams-core

contexts.description: Interactive modal that renders a template's use-case flows as a node-edge flow diagram. Supports multi-flow navigation via tab bar, node inspection via popover, and smart popover positioning relative to the canvas viewport. Consumes UseCaseFlow JSON stored in PersonaDesignReview.use_case_flows.
contexts.name: template-activity-diagrams

contexts.description: Top-level adoption wizard orchestrator: AdoptionWizardModal is the outer shell (modal or inline) that resets stale build sessions and confirms before discarding in-progress work. ChronologyAdoptionView drives the full adoption lifecycle (session creation, questionnaire, build). ChronologyCommandHub and TestReportModal handle post-adoption use-case command visibility and test reports.
contexts.name: template-adoption-chronology

contexts.description: Spec verifying the post-fix DOM signature of the adoption wizard's Persona Layout tab: scroll container bounding, layout switcher class, and credential modal reachability. Diagnostic-first design — asserts what is live in the running bundle rather than driving a full adoption flow.
contexts.name: template-adoption-e2e

contexts.description: Matrix-style adoption surface that shows all 8 persona dimensions as a petal layout, letting the user review and edit each capability, error policy, schedule, and connector binding before creating. useAdoptionDimensionModel is the orchestration hook that maintains petal states, maps questionnaire answers to dimensions, and drives inline editing.
contexts.name: template-adoption-persona-layout

contexts.description: Multi-question interview UI that walks the user through configuring a template's 8 adoption dimensions. Each question maps to a glyph dimension and renders as a hero question with stacked options, a story thread, category rail, footer navigation, and keyboard shortcuts. Tracks category progress and surfaces blocked-credential CTAs when required connectors are missing.
contexts.name: template-adoption-questionnaire

contexts.description: Supporting utilities and cross-cutting components for the adoption flow: vault-to-question credential matching (vaultAdoptionMatcher), dynamic question option resolution, hydrated design result loading, shared use-case trigger normalisation, composition x-ray inspector, messaging picker, pill selectors, questionnaire form grid, glyph animations, and the quick-add credential modal.
contexts.name: template-adoption-support

contexts.description: Core use-case picker shell that lets users select how a template will be activated (schedule, event, cockpit, forge). The panel hosts route toggles, a card-based selection grid, and the cockpit/power-rail views. useUcPickerState manages the picker's internal tab and selection state, and ucPickerHelpers provides normalization utilities.
contexts.name: template-adoption-uc-picker-core

contexts.description: Specialised visual variants for the use-case picker: notification glyphs (stamp, in-app, app-notification), deliver card, forge editor, preview modal, time-aware cards and controls (clock variant, time card, time controls). Each variant represents a distinct way the template persona can be scheduled or triggered in production.
contexts.name: template-adoption-uc-picker-variants

contexts.description: Loads, verifies, validates, and localizes the built-in persona template library at runtime. Templates are lazily fetched via Vite glob imports from scripts/templates/, verified against embedded SHA checksums (client-side fast path) and the Rust binary (authoritative async path), then validated for schema correctness before admission. Per-language overlay files supply translated user-facing strings without duplicating structural data. The useLocalizedTemplateCatalog React hook makes the catalog available to UI components, automatically refreshing on language change.
contexts.name: template-catalog

contexts.description: Read-only preview of an AI-generated template's design result, broken into three sections: connectors pipeline, event subscriptions, and messaging channels. Also includes the design summary bar, a test-results panel that shows validation scores per dimension, and a checkbox to flag specific dimensions for re-generation.
contexts.name: template-design-preview

contexts.description: Two-level domain explorer that presents automation templates grouped into business domains. Level 1 is a bento-grid mosaic of 7 domains; level 2 drills into a domain's templates and recipes. Reads from useExploreCatalog which merges the template gallery with the recipe index to produce a unified exploration surface.
contexts.name: template-explore-view

contexts.description: Interactive card-layer elements: the virtual scrolling list, row-level action menu, connector icon buttons, expanded row details, compare tray, review cache, and all hooks driving card data and comparison state. GeneratedReviewsTab is the root gallery host that wires together search, filters, virtual list, and modals.
contexts.name: template-gallery-card-actions

contexts.description: Rendering layer for individual template cards in the gallery list. TemplateCard is the top-level polymorphic renderer that delegates to header, body, footer, and preview sub-components based on density mode. Also includes category icon mapping and category pill badges used across all card densities.
contexts.name: template-gallery-card-renderers

contexts.description: Discovery section within the generated gallery: trending and recommended template carousels, role-group category cards, an automation opportunities rail (AI-generated suggestions tied to the active persona), background decorative banners, and an empty-state family for zero-result and AI-search modes.
contexts.name: template-gallery-explore

contexts.description: Modal layer for the template gallery: detail view, preview, rebuild, multi-template compare, recommended picks, credential quick-setup, and the use-cases tab. useModalStack manages a push/pop stack so modals can open sub-modals without losing their parent. TemplateModals is the root compositor that renders whichever modal is currently active.
contexts.name: template-gallery-modals

contexts.description: Full search and filter bar for the template gallery: structured query chips, AI-powered autocomplete suggestions, connector/component/sort/density/admin filter dropdowns, and a filter chip row. useStructuredQuery converts free-text input into typed query chips (keyword, connector, tag, use-case) that the virtual list filters against.
contexts.name: template-gallery-search

contexts.description: Three-step AI wizard for creating a new template from scratch: Describe (name + description input), Generate (invokes the design runner via IPC and streams progress), and Review (shows the generated design result for approval). State is managed by a wizard reducer with snapshot persistence so the wizard can survive navigations.
contexts.name: template-generation

contexts.description: Persona template adoption and discovery — adopting a community or built-in template onto a persona, capturing user feedback on templates, semantic smart-search across the template library, and archetype definitions (the 9 pre-built persona composition building blocks).
contexts.name: template-library

contexts.description: Shared primitives for the template-marathon E2E harness: adoption-phase helpers (open modal, seed questionnaire answers, switch variants, wait for build phases, cancel sessions), execution polling, and low-level HTTP plumbing. Also exports countToolSteps and waitForExecution for the marathon spec.
contexts.name: template-marathon-bridge

contexts.description: Full end-to-end Playwright spec for adopting a single template: open picker, seed questionnaire, build, promote, execute, and verify the execution completed with tool steps. Driven by the Node driver (template-marathon-driver.mjs) once per template id, writing per-template JSON results to tests/results/marathon/. Rescore script aggregates pass/fail.
contexts.name: template-marathon-e2e

contexts.description: Template inventory and vault-matching logic for the marathon harness. Loads all template JSON files from the repo, parses adoption questions, classifies vault-credential questions (which must NOT be seeded), and provides DEFAULT_VAULT matching so the driver knows which templates the user's vault can actually adopt.
contexts.name: template-marathon-fixtures

contexts.description: Top-level page container for the Templates section that hosts five tab-routed sub-views (generated gallery, n8n import, explore, recipes, presets). It reads the active tab from the system store, composes sub-feature components behind ErrorBoundary guards, and manages the activity-diagram modal that shows use-case flow visualisations. Depends on useDesignReviews hook and vaultStore/systemStore for credential/tab state.
contexts.name: template-page-shell

contexts.description: Team preset library that surfaces filesystem-shipped multi-persona team configurations. PresetLibraryPage renders presets as a data-weighted bento mosaic (tile size scales with team size). PresetPreviewModal shows a graph preview and adoption flow; PresetQuestionnaireForm and usePresetAdoption handle configuring the preset before deployment.
contexts.name: template-presets

contexts.description: Hooks for browsing the template gallery, querying gallery items, generating recipes from AI, executing and versioning recipes, managing design review cycles, and driving AI artifact flows. These hooks power the template/recipe picker and the recipe refinement surface inside the Design & Build Studio.
contexts.name: template-recipe-hooks

contexts.description: Reusable building blocks shared across template sub-features: BaseModal overlay, ThinkingLoader spinner, TrustBadge scan indicator, ConnectorReadiness readiness chip, ConnectorPipeline visualisation, DimensionRadial chart, AdoptCelebration confetti, SandboxWarningBanner, ScanResultsBanner, TeamSynthesisPanel, and library utilities (adoptionReadiness, architecturalCategories, templateComplexity, vaultAdoptionMatcher).
contexts.name: template-shared-primitives

contexts.description: Reusable terminal-output UI components shared across features that display CLI or log output: CliOutputPanel (panel wrapping stdout/stderr streams), TerminalBody (scrollable xterm-style output body), TerminalHeader (title bar with controls), TerminalSearchBar (filter/search within output), and TerminalStrip (compact inline strip for activity teasers). These are generic display shells; actual stream data comes from callers.
contexts.name: terminal-ui

contexts.description: Core HTTP harness that drives the real Tauri app via the test-automation server on port 17320. The CompanionBridge class wraps /query, /click-testid, /bridge-exec and other primitives into a typed API that all Playwright specs share. Also exports the ALL_TOUR_IDS registry and shared type definitions for panel state, brain counts, and tour snapshots.
contexts.name: test-bridge-core

contexts.description: Generates LLM-driven test scenarios for personas and runs them against model variants in the Lab. The test_runner module spawns Claude CLI in headless mode to generate and execute test scenarios with TTL-based caching; eval drives structured evaluation runs; output_assertions checks execution outputs against declared assertions; verification_command provides a structured command type for post-execution verification steps.
contexts.name: test-runner-lab

contexts.description: Repositories for persona test suites, test runs, assertions, and knowledge base quality gating. Allows users to define expected behavior tests that run against persona executions, with structured assertion results. The `quality_gate` module enforces pass/fail criteria before execution can be promoted.
contexts.name: testing-quality-repo

contexts.description: Hooks for platform-level display concerns: resolving a persona's visual vibe/theme, detecting document visibility for pause-on-hide optimizations, checking whether a DOM element is in the viewport, classifying terminal output lines by semantic type, and providing time-of-day context for adaptive UI. These hooks are used by multiple features with no single owner.
contexts.name: theming-platform-hooks

contexts.description: Low-level timing and scheduling primitives: debounce for text input, debounced-save combining debounce with persist calls, elapsed timer for duration display, polling loops with configurable interval and backoff, RAF-coalesced callback scheduling to batch rapid updates into single animation frames, animated number interpolation for smooth counters, and a relative-time ticker for live 'X ago' labels.
contexts.name: timing-utility-hooks

contexts.description: Handles virtual tool dispatch during persona execution: built-in tools (filesystem, shell, search), MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools via stdio/SSE transport with session pooling, and dry-run preview that assembles the full prompt and tool surface without spawning a real subprocess. Acts as the tool execution broker between the runner and external capability providers.
contexts.name: tool-execution

contexts.description: Direct tool invocation panel that lets a developer call a specific tool bound to a persona without triggering a full execution. ToolRunnerModal and ToolRunnerPanel compose the UI; ToolInvocationCard renders each invocation result; useToolRunner manages the IPC request/response cycle.
contexts.name: tool-runner

contexts.description: Repositories for tool definitions, connector definitions, and connector-readiness resolution. Manages the catalog of available tools and third-party service integrations that personas can use. Includes persona-tool bindings, connector credential associations, and healthcheck configurations.
contexts.name: tools-connectors-repo

contexts.api_surface: list_tools, create_tool, list_automations, deploy_automation, list_triggers, create_trigger
contexts.description: CRUD and lifecycle management for tools (callable functions/integrations) and automation pipelines attached to personas. Covers automation design (AI-assisted generation), deployment, and trigger wiring. The triggers module manages event→automation bindings.
contexts.name: tools-management

contexts.description: TTS narration bridge that speaks each guided-tour step via the companion's ElevenLabs/Piper voice pipeline when the user has voice configured. useTourNarration is a purely additive hook — it never blocks step advancement and silently no-ops when no voice is set up. Results are cached per step-id to avoid redundant synth calls; the orb glow reacts to narration audio through the shared analyser pipeline.
contexts.name: tour-narration

contexts.description: The body content area of the tour panel, including step navigation, sub-step checklist, the 'Show me' focus-scroll affordance, step progress breadcrumbs, and the tour intro card shown on first entry. TourPanelBody dispatches between generic informational content (for tours 2+) and specialized interactive components (TourAppearanceContent, CredentialsTourContent, PersonaCreationCoach) for the Getting Started tour. TourHandoffOffer is a one-time card bridging the onboarding modal completion into the tour.
contexts.name: tour-panel-ui

contexts.description: SVG-based screen dimming overlay with an animated rectangular cut-out that tracks a live DOM element by data-testid. TourSpotlight uses the shared useTrackedElementRect hook for measurement and MutationObserver-backed re-measurement; when the target can't be found it sets a 'highlightMissing' flag so the panel shows a contextual note rather than dismissing the whole tour.
contexts.name: tour-spotlight

contexts.description: Three lazy-loaded specialized content components for the Getting Started tour's interactive steps. TourAppearanceContent renders live theme/brightness controls inside the tour panel. CredentialsTourContent guides vault credential setup. PersonaCreationCoach mirrors the multi-agent build engine's real-time phase state (analyzing → resolving → draft_ready → promoted) as an inline coaching checklist with matrix dimension progress.
contexts.name: tour-step-content

contexts.api_surface: Injected TriagePorts: reviewAction, acceptIdea, rejectIdea, decideKnowledge, submitAnswers, createTask
contexts.description: The pure, React-free business logic layer for the unified triage system. Defines the `TriageItem` discriminated union that every source domain (reviews, ideas, practices, questions) adapts to, the queue projection logic (resolved removal, skip ordering, kind filtering), the verdict-to-backend-write router, adopt-reach computation, and the i18n-injected adapter functions that convert raw domain rows into `TriageItem` instances.
contexts.name: triage-core

contexts.description: The full-app swipe deck that replaced the 576px anchored popover. Shows one card at a time from the unified queue with drag-to-decide physics ported from the existing `SwipeCard` / `BacklogFocusDeck` — reviewers already know the gesture. Includes the deck chrome (top bar with filter chips and progress, action bar with flanks, loading and cleared states), the `TriageCard` (draggable verdict card with markdown body, facts ledger, tags, alert banner, and branch buttons), and `QuestionPanel` (non-draggable, collects answers for build-question items). Keyboard: arrows decide, digit keys fire branches, Escape skips.
contexts.name: triage-deck-ui

contexts.api_surface: createFinding, setVerifyState, sweepFindings via devTools API
contexts.description: The findings engine automates discovery and triage of development issues by sweeping multiple sensor sources (Sentry errors, off-track KPIs, context coverage gaps) and writing deduped FindingDraft records to dev_ideas. emitters produce typed drafts per sensor; dispatch persists them; verify re-measures shipped findings to clear or regress their status; sensorStats and healthIngest feed the Sensor Scoreboard UI.
contexts.name: triage-findings

contexts.description: Triage rules panel that lets operators configure which findings categories to accept and with what effort/risk thresholds. TriageRulesPanel renders the rule list; EffortRiskFilter provides the effort × risk slider controls; triageRuleSuggestions generates AI-suggested rules based on project history.
contexts.name: triage-rules

contexts.description: Unit and render-cost tests for the triage core logic and deck controls. Covers adapter correctness (domain rows → TriageItem), dispatch routing (every verdict × kind combination, including the deferral guard for question rejections), queue projection (skip ordering, kind filtering, resolved exclusion), reach computation, and a render-cost benchmark asserting that the deck does not re-render card markdown on every keystroke.
contexts.name: triage-tests

contexts.description: The `useUnifiedTriage` React hook that fuses four independent 'a human must decide' data sources — persona manual reviews, build/adoption questions, backlog ideas, and workspace practices — into a single sorted queue. Manages per-session skip ledger, resolved-item optimistic removal, kind-filter toggles, idea pagination, and a `decide` dispatcher that writes to the correct backend. The hook is the seam between the pure core logic and React state.
contexts.name: triage-unified-hook

contexts.description: Configuration panels for every supported trigger type (webhook, polling, file-watcher, event-listener, app-focus, clipboard, composite). Includes the config dispatcher buildTriggerConfig and each type-specific form component, plus shared field-group layout. Used inside TriggerDetailDrawer and TriggerAddForm.
contexts.name: trigger-config

contexts.description: Visual health and status indicators for individual triggers: health sparklines, health dots, arm state badge, dry-run result view. Provides at-a-glance feedback on trigger reliability and recent execution outcome.
contexts.name: trigger-health-indicators

contexts.description: Per-persona trigger list UI: creating, viewing, toggling, deleting, and detail-drilling triggers. Includes the add form with NL input support, trigger rows, the detail drawer, quick templates, type/category selectors, and execution history per trigger. The core CRUD surface users interact with inside each persona.
contexts.name: trigger-list-management

contexts.description: Centralised React hooks for trigger CRUD, validation, test-fire, dry-run, and execution history fetch. useTriggerOperations provides a uniform {ok, data?, error?} result shape for all trigger mutations. useTriggerHistory and useTriggerDetail offer read-oriented query hooks.
contexts.name: trigger-operations-hook

contexts.description: Schedule/time-based configuration for triggers: timezone selector, active-hours windowing, unattended-mode section, countdown ring, schedule preview, and schedule config form. Handles cron-style and interval-based scheduling UX.
contexts.name: trigger-schedule

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: list_triggers, create_trigger, start_scheduler, backfill_missed_runs, get_workflows_overview, cancel_workflow_job
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for persona trigger management (cron schedules, webhooks, event-based firings) and the background scheduler that orchestrates them. Triggers define when a persona runs autonomously; the scheduler controls start/stop/backfill and reports missed runs. Workflow job management (listing, cancelling, reading output of background CI-style jobs) is also included.
contexts.name: trigger-scheduler-api

contexts.description: Chain Studio — a visual patchbay UI for creating and managing event-routing rules between personas. Users compose draft 'patch cable' routes (source event → target persona), set run conditions (always/success/failure/output_match), and commit them as live trigger bindings. Supersedes the older builder + routes views.
contexts.name: trigger-studio

contexts.description: Manual trigger test-fire tab: lets users fire a test event against a selected trigger to validate it without waiting for the real schedule or event. Surfaces validation errors and the resulting execution.
contexts.name: trigger-test-tab

contexts.description: Repositories for event triggers, automation rules, and webhook configurations that cause personas to execute. Stores trigger definitions (cron, webhook, event-based), automation pipelines, and cloud webhook watermarks for deduplication during event replay.
contexts.name: triggers-automations-repo

contexts.description: The top-level shell for the Event Bus / Triggers section. It owns the tab-switcher between all sub-tabs (live-stream, rate-limits, test, smee-relay, cloud-webhooks, dead-letter, studio, shared) and fetches the global trigger health map on mount. Depends on pipelineStore, agentStore, and systemStore for tab routing.
contexts.name: triggers-page-shell

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_twin_profile, update_twin_profile, list_twin_channels, compile_twin_wiki, list_twin_pending_memories
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for the Digital Twin plugin: managing a user's twin profile (tone, voice, personality), twin channels (Slack, email, Telegram delivery), pending memory approval queue, outbound communications log, contacts, wiki compilation (building a knowledge document from twin facts), distilled facts, studio batch runs, and reflections. The twin acts as the user's AI representative across communication channels.
contexts.name: twin-api

contexts.api_surface: knowledge base CRUD + bind/unbind via twinApi
contexts.description: Knowledge-base and memory connectivity layer for a twin, visualised as a two-layer cortex: Layer 1 is an optional Obsidian vault subpath binding; Layer 2 is a searchable knowledge base (create, bind, or link existing). Also hosts three sub-panels — distilled facts, semantic recall preview, and twin reflections — tabbed below the KB connection UI.
contexts.name: twin-brain

contexts.api_surface: twin channel CRUD + activity query via systemStore/twinApi
contexts.description: Deployment channel management for a twin: create, activate/pause, and delete channel bindings (email, LinkedIn, Slack, Twitter, etc.) with credential linking and tone binding. Includes an activity-staleness tracker, a reply outbox for staged outbound messages, and a sent-replies log with reuse affordances.
contexts.name: twin-channels

contexts.description: Two-spec end-to-end suite for the Discord Twin plugin: setup spec provisions a real Discord credential via the Connections UI and creates a Twin persona with inbound polling config; replier spec runs the actual message-receive and reply cycle. Requires DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN and DISCORD_TEST_CHANNEL_ID env vars.
contexts.name: twin-discord-e2e

contexts.description: Identity configuration sub-page for a digital twin, covering bio, pronouns, languages, and role fields. The atelier wraps an identity form with contextual guidance on how bio length affects the readiness score. Writes back to the active twin profile via systemStore.
contexts.name: twin-identity

contexts.api_surface: memory approve/reject/defer + doctrine ingest via twinApi
contexts.description: Memory inbox for a twin: incoming communications surface as pending memories for user approval, rejection (with preset reasons), or deferral. Approved memories feed the readiness score. Also exposes a contacts panel and a wiki-style ingestion flow for loading doctrine documents into the brain.
contexts.name: twin-knowledge-memory

contexts.description: Digital twin profile management including a constellation-style atelier UI with a hero card for the active twin and satellite cards for others. Handles CRUD (create via wizard, inline edit, delete with confirmation) and aggregates per-profile readiness scores and KPIs across the roster. Relies on useTwinReadiness and useProfileDashboards for derived state.
contexts.name: twin-profiles

contexts.description: Shared presentational components and utility modules used across all Twin sub-pages. Includes the unified TwinHeaderBand (gradient hero band with KPI slots, readiness ribbon, and decoration prop), the ReadinessGapPopover and gap-ranking logic, a TwinPicker selector, channel palette definitions, gender-sigil helpers, and decorative SVG elements.
contexts.name: twin-shared-ui

contexts.description: Entry point and routing layer for the Twin plugin. Manages tab routing across seven sub-pages, hydratesactive-twin data layers on twin change, and drives a readiness-celebration effect when a milestone closes. Depends on systemStore for active twin state and lazy-loads each sub-page for code splitting.
contexts.name: twin-shell

contexts.description: Unit tests for the Twin plugin's core logic. Covers the useTwinReadiness hook's milestone-status derivation and scoring algorithm across all combinations of profile, tone, channel, and memory states.
contexts.name: twin-tests

contexts.api_surface: twin tones CRUD via twinApi + systemStore
contexts.description: Voice and tone configuration for a twin's communication style across channels. The atelier presents a left rail of channel stations (generic, email, LinkedIn, Slack, etc.) and a centre stage card for editing voice directives, message examples, constraints, and length hints per channel. Includes an AI auto-suggest flow and a console view for quick inline edits.
contexts.name: twin-tone

contexts.api_surface: AI question generation + memory save via twinApi
contexts.description: Interview-style training sessions that teach a twin how to respond by collecting Q&A pairs across six topic categories (background, opinions, communication, values, expertise, personal). An AI generates contextual follow-up questions; answers are saved as approved memories. Includes topic-coverage scoring, a momentum tracker, and a training studio for extended sessions.
contexts.name: twin-training

contexts.description: Variant tab strip component for switching between twin variants within the Twin plugin. Renders a compact tab bar used by pages that surface multiple view modes or twin variants side-by-side.
contexts.name: twin-variant-tabs

contexts.description: Hooks for UI motion, progressive disclosure, accessibility, and save-state feedback: a motion preference hook respecting prefers-reduced-motion, progressive reveal animations for list items, tracked element rect for anchor-positioned overlays, roving tab-index for keyboard navigation, async action state management, unsaved-change guards, save feedback toasts, settings-save toasts, and tier-gating checks. Shared across many feature surfaces.
contexts.name: ui-animation-hooks

contexts.description: Collapsible audit trail showing both Personas Cloud and GitLab deployment/sync history rows in a unified list ordered by recency. Fetches the combined history via list_deployment_history_all query when expanded, renders target badges, rollback indicators, and prompt-snapshot icons per row, and applies the standard one-shot entrance cascade pattern for smooth appearance.
contexts.name: unified-deployment-history

contexts.description: Sanitizes URLs (blocking private network ranges, unsafe protocols, embedded credentials, and unicode bidi overrides) and HTML (using DOMPurify, allowing only highlight.js span tags) before rendering in the UI. Prevents SSRF, tracking pixels, and XSS from AI-generated or external content.
contexts.name: url-html-sanitization

contexts.description: Unit tests for the shared utility layer, covering terminal line classification, formatter edge cases, safeInvoke command-not-found detection, URL sanitization, and prompt injection stripping. These tests act as a regression guard for security-sensitive primitives that have no higher-level integration tests.
contexts.name: utils-tests

contexts.api_surface: Tauri IPC: run_api_test; calls external connector APIs via credential
contexts.description: Interactive API playground modal shell for testing connector credentials against live endpoints. CredentialPlaygroundModal is the root; PlaygroundHeader shows connector identity; RequestBuilder and BuilderParams construct HTTP requests; ResponseViewer renders the raw response; EndpointRow lists available endpoints; useApiTestRunner drives the request execution and response state.
contexts.name: vault-api-playground-shell

contexts.description: Tab views within the API playground modal: Overview (connector summary, health), API Explorer (endpoint list, request firing, response viewer), MCP Tools (list/invoke MCP tools per server), Executions (recent test runs), and recipe creation flow. useApiExplorerState manages the explorer tab's selected endpoint and response history.
contexts.name: vault-api-playground-tabs

contexts.description: Session management and adapter layer for the automated credential (AutoCred) Playwright-driven flow. useAutoCredSession maintains the phase FSM, extracted values, browser log entries, and adapter results. TauriPlaywrightAdapter wraps Playwright MCP calls into a swappable interface; helper functions handle error parsing and field completeness checks.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-autocred-session

contexts.api_surface: Playwright MCP: playwright_navigate, playwright_snapshot, playwright_fill, playwright_click
contexts.description: Automated credential harvesting UI that drives a Playwright browser session to extract API keys from a service's developer portal. The wizard walks through Consent→Browser→Review steps; AutoCredPanel is the root; BrowserDetail shows the live Playwright session; AutoCredReview lets the user confirm extracted values before saving.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-autocred-ui

contexts.description: AI-driven credential design modal that analyzes a URL or service description and proposes a connector configuration. The modal walks through Idle→Analyzing→Preview→Done phases (each a separate component), shows recipe confidence banners, and renders setup instructions. CredentialDesignContext provides the orchestrator value to all phase components via context.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-design-modal

contexts.description: Orchestrator logic and setup instruction rendering for the AI credential design flow. useCredentialDesignOrchestrator composes useCredentialDesign, useOAuthConsent, useUniversalOAuth, and useCredentialHealth into a single context value. Setup instruction helpers render markdown-formatted step-by-step guides fetched from the backend design result.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-design-orchestrator

contexts.description: Desktop app and local MCP server discovery panel. DesktopDiscoveryPanel scans the user's machine for installed apps (DesktopAppCard, DiscoveryAppList) and running MCP servers (McpServerCard, DiscoveryMcpList). CapabilityApprovalCard surfaces per-capability permission grants required before connecting a locally discovered service.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-desktop

contexts.description: Credential foraging feature that scans the user's environment (shell config, dotfiles, cloud CLIs) for existing credentials that can be auto-imported. ForagingPanel orchestrates the scan; ForagingConsent gates the operation behind user approval; ForagingResults and ForagingResultCard present discovered secrets; ForagingStepIndicator shows scan progress.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-foraging

contexts.description: Catalog-level credential template forms for creating connector credentials from a pre-defined template. CredentialTemplateForm is the main form; CredentialTypePicker selects the connector type; CodebaseProjectPicker and ProjectList handle project-scoped connectors; TemplateFormBody renders the field layout.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-forms

contexts.description: AI-guided connector setup negotiator that interactively walks a user through multi-step configuration. NegotiatorPanel is the root; NegotiatorPhases renders Guiding or Planning phases; NegotiatorStepCard shows each step with its status; StepActions provides approve/skip/retry controls. negotiatorMotion defines the animation presets for step transitions.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-negotiator

contexts.description: The main connector catalog grid that lets users browse, search, and filter available connector types before adding a credential. CredentialPicker is the root; PickerGrid renders connector cards; CredentialPickerFilters provides role-based and category filtering; usePickerFilters drives filter state; useRecipeIndicators shows which connectors already have recipes.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-picker

contexts.description: Connector schema-driven form rendering. CredentialSchemaForm renders a dynamic form from a connector's JSON auth schema; SchemaFormFields maps schema field types to React inputs; ExtraFieldRenderers handles non-standard field types; McpPrefilledForm pre-fills known MCP server fields; schemaConfigs centralizes per-connector field overrides.
contexts.name: vault-catalog-schemas

contexts.description: Credential card-level status indicators and action banners. CompositeHealthDot renders a multi-signal health dot; ReauthBanner prompts re-authentication when a token is revoked; ScopeMismatchBanner warns when a saved credential lacks required scopes; VaultErrorBanner surfaces vault-level errors; CredentialDeleteDialog handles soft-delete with undo.
contexts.name: vault-credential-card-banners

contexts.description: Credential intelligence panels displayed in the credential detail view. Covers anomaly score display, audit log table, scope section, event template configuration, and the CredentialIntelligence aggregate panel. These surfaces give operators visibility into credential usage patterns and abnormal activity detected by the backend.
contexts.name: vault-credential-health-intel

contexts.description: Multi-step credential import wizard that lets users bulk-import secrets from files, cloud secret managers, or other external sources. ImportSourcePicker selects the source type; ImportInputPhase handles raw input; ImportPreview shows a diff before committing; ImportSyncConfig configures ongoing sync; useCredentialImport drives the wizard state machine.
contexts.name: vault-credential-import

contexts.description: Reusable resource picker component that appears after saving a credential, allowing users to immediately link the new credential to a cloud resource (e.g. a specific S3 bucket or GitHub repo). resourcePickerStore is a lightweight Zustand slice holding picker visibility and target state; usePostSaveResourcePicker bridges the save flow to picker open.
contexts.name: vault-credential-resource-picker

contexts.description: Credential secret rotation UI. CredentialRotationSection is the main detail panel showing rotation history and anomaly score; RotationPolicyControls, RotationNewPolicy, and RotationActivePolicy manage creating and viewing rotation schedules; RotationCountdownRing renders a visual countdown timer to the next scheduled rotation.
contexts.name: vault-credential-rotation

contexts.description: Team and workspace credential sharing surfaces. GatewayMembersModal manages which team members have access to a shared gateway credential; PendingAuthModal handles pending authorization requests from collaborators. WorkspaceConnectPanel and ProviderSection enable connecting workspace providers (GitHub, Slack, Google Workspace) so their credentials are shared across a team.
contexts.name: vault-credential-team-access

contexts.description: Credential creation and editing forms, covering auth-method tabs (API key, OAuth, basic, MCP), field capture rows, connection-test section, OAuth progress ring, and setup guide. ConnectorCredentialModal is the primary modal; CredentialEditForm handles the form state. Renders different field renderers depending on the connector's authentication schema.
contexts.name: vault-credentials-form

contexts.description: Credential list view with column definitions, filtering, detail modal wiring, and empty state. CredentialList renders the sortable/filterable table of stored credentials; CredentialListColumns defines the column schema (name, connector, health status, last-used); useCredentialListFilters provides client-side search and filter logic.
contexts.name: vault-credentials-list

contexts.description: Top-level credential manager shell that coordinates the full credential management workflow. Orchestrates the credential list, add-views, breadcrumb navigation, trust badge, rotate-all action, undo-delete, and re-auth banner. useCredentialManagerState drives the FSM (list / add / detail views) via a reducer dispatch; CredentialManagerViews renders the active view.
contexts.name: vault-credentials-manager

contexts.description: Slice managing encrypted credential storage — listing, creating, updating, deleting, and healthchecking credential records and their associated connectors. Implements a 30-second cached fetch to deduplicate concurrent IPC calls from multiple components, with optimistic mutations and tombstone-based delete protection.
contexts.name: vault-credentials-state

contexts.description: AI-assisted SQL chat tab inside the database explorer. ChatTab is the container; ChatMessages renders the conversation history; ChatInput handles user queries; AssistantSqlBlock renders AI-generated SQL with syntax highlighting and a one-click 'run in editor' action. The AI interprets schema context to generate contextually correct queries.
contexts.name: vault-database-chat

contexts.description: SQL query editor pane and console tab within the database explorer. QueryEditorPane hosts the editor + toolbar; QueryToolbar provides run/format/safe-mode controls; QuerySidebar shows saved queries; QueriesTab is the tab container; ConsoleTab and ConsoleOutput show query execution logs; ResultsTable renders query results; MutationConfirmBanner guards destructive queries.
contexts.name: vault-database-query-editor

contexts.description: Core database connector explorer shell. DatabaseListView lists all database-type credentials; DatabaseCard renders a card per database with connection status; DBGrid is the main explorer host; SchemaManagerModal browses database schema; SqlEditor is the CodeMirror-based SQL input; introspectionQueries defines per-dialect schema queries; safeModeUtils and sqlTokenizers support safe-mode filtering.
contexts.name: vault-database-shell

contexts.description: Slice for database connector management — tracking configured database connections (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, etc.) that agent personas can query. Manages connection testing, schema discovery, and table listing for the Database Explorer feature.
contexts.name: vault-database-state

contexts.description: Table and column browser within the database explorer. TablesTab lists all tables; TableListSidebar provides sidebar navigation; TableDetailPanel shows column details and row preview; ColumnList renders columns with types; TableSearch enables fuzzy search; TableActions and TableContextMenu provide table-level operations; ConnectorCapabilityNote surfaces capability limitations.
contexts.name: vault-database-table-browser

contexts.description: Test suite for the database explorer sub-feature. Covers ChatTab integration, ConnectorCapabilityNote rendering, DatabaseCard and DatabaseListView display, introspection query parity across dialects, introspection query correctness, QueryResultTable, SchemaManagerModal, and SqlEditor behavior.
contexts.name: vault-database-tests

contexts.description: Interactive credential relationship graph showing how credentials are connected to personas, recipes, and other credentials. CredentialRelationshipGraph is the root; GraphCanvas renders a force-directed D3 layout; BlastRadiusPanel shows impact analysis when a credential is revoked; SimulationPanel and SimulationControls let the user model revocation scenarios; credentialGraph.ts contains the pure graph algorithms.
contexts.name: vault-dependency-graph

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: scan_credential_sources, import_foraged_credential, start_credential_negotiation, create_knowledge_base, kb_search, kb_ingest_file
contexts.description: IPC wrappers for AI-powered vault intelligence features: credential foraging (scanning system sources like browser keychains and env files to discover importable credentials), AI credential negotiation (guided step-by-step field collection for complex connectors), and the vector knowledge base (CRUD, semantic search, document ingestion, entity extraction, and embedding-backed retrieval). These features layer intelligent assistance over the raw credential and knowledge stores.
contexts.name: vault-intelligence-api

contexts.description: Top-level vault UI entry points shared across the credential and catalog sub-features. Provides the VaultConnectorPicker for selecting connectors, CredentialPickerCards for card-style credential selection, and SetupStatusBadge to surface connector setup progress. Consumed by agent editors and other features that need to attach a credential.
contexts.name: vault-root-components

contexts.description: Slices managing credential rotation policies, automation workflows tied to credentials, and catalog UI preferences (filters, sort order, view mode). The rotation slice tracks scheduled and on-demand rotation jobs; the rotationOverview selector derives summary stats for the catalog header.
contexts.name: vault-rotation-state

contexts.api_surface: Wraps IPC: vaultStatus, credential health, bulk healthcheck, OAuth consent
contexts.description: Cross-cutting React hooks shared by all vault sub-features. Covers credential OAuth flows (Google, universal), credential renaming, tag management, undo-delete, rotation ticker, vault status polling with module-level IPC cache, credential view FSM, navigation context, and the three-state health-check system (bulk healthcheck, per-credential health, and remediation evaluator). Acts as the primary shared hook library for vault UI state.
contexts.name: vault-shared-hooks

contexts.description: Pure utility functions used throughout the vault feature. Provides auth-method style maps (icon, color, label per auth type), a three-state credential health score calculator, and tag normalization helpers. Also contains the unit test suite for the health score logic.
contexts.name: vault-shared-utils

contexts.description: Top-level Zustand store composing the vault domain — credentials, database connectors, automations, rotation policies, and catalog UI preferences. Provides the unified store interface for all secrets management and connector features.
contexts.name: vault-store-root

contexts.description: Document ingestion and entity extraction UI for the vector knowledge base. IngestDropZone and IngestDirectoryPicker handle file/folder input; IngestProgressBar shows chunking/embedding progress; IngestTextModal accepts pasted text; EntityTable and SchemaEditor support structured extraction of entities from ingested documents into typed tables.
contexts.name: vault-vector-kb-ingest

contexts.description: Vector knowledge base modal shell and tab surfaces for credentials that back a knowledge base (e.g. a file store). VectorKbModal is the root 4-tab modal (Documents, Search, Extract, Settings); tabs handle document listing, semantic search, entity extraction, settings configuration, and corpus overview; StatusBadge shows KB indexing state.
contexts.name: vault-vector-kb-shell

contexts.description: Manages the sqlite-vec virtual table used for semantic vector search over knowledge base chunks. Handles vec0 extension registration, embedding storage, approximate nearest-neighbor queries, and the BM25 FTS5 re-ranker. ML-feature-gated; only compiled when the `ml` cargo feature is enabled.
contexts.name: vector-store
