contexts.description: UI interaction primitives for scroll and viewport management: click-outside detection, clipboard copy with keyed flag tracking, infinite-scroll end-reached detection, compact-mode detection, mobile preview toggling, virtual list windowing for large datasets, viewport clamping to keep popovers in-bounds, scroll shadow indicators, and scroll position restoration across navigation. Used by shared components and feature panels alike.
contexts.name: viewport-interaction-hooks

contexts.description: Parses structured protocol markers emitted by Athena in build-turn replies (`BUILD_PLAN: {json}` and `NEEDS_INPUT: <question|json>`), strips them from the user-visible reply, and surfaces the build phase checklist and any pending decision the user must resolve. Also builds per-turn MCP connector configs (Context7, Playwright) that Claude Code loads via `--mcp-config` during build turns.
contexts.name: webbuild-build-turn

contexts.description: Locates and invokes the Bun runtime sidecar used by the Athena web-dev companion for all shell-out operations (scaffold, install, build). Resolves the Bun binary via `PERSONAS_BUN_BIN` env override or PATH lookup, then runs one-shot bounded commands capturing stdout/stderr. Also provides the `hide_window` helper used by both one-shot and long-lived spawn paths to suppress console flicker on Windows.
contexts.name: webbuild-bun-runtime

contexts.description: Supervises long-lived `bun run dev` servers for web-build projects, one per project, tracked in an in-memory registry keyed by project ID. Provides start/stop/status/list operations and ensures the full process tree (including child Next.js/node processes) is killed on stop or app exit. Health-checks the server by probing for a real HTTP response rather than a bare TCP connect, so a bound-but-stalled server is never reported healthy.
contexts.name: webbuild-devserver

contexts.api_surface: list_routes(dir); commit_snapshot(dir, summary); list_versions(dir); restore(dir, sha); preview_agent::ensure(dir)
contexts.description: Provides the three preview-layer primitives for Athena Studio: (1) Next.js app-router route discovery by scanning `app/` for `page.*` files, used to populate the Studio navigation bar; (2) per-turn git snapshot commit and restore for the version history timeline; and (3) injection of the `AthenaPreviewAgent` TSX component into the generated project's root layout, enabling cross-origin `postMessage` element-location and route-reporting from inside the preview iframe back to the Studio host.
contexts.name: webbuild-preview

contexts.description: Manages the lifecycle of Athena-generated web projects stored under `~/.personas/projects/<slug>/`. Handles slug generation from human names, path-traversal-safe directory resolution, and scaffolding a blank Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind app via `bun x create-next-app`, including pinning the Turbopack workspace root to prevent stray parent lockfile interference.
contexts.name: webbuild-project-scaffold

contexts.description: Inbound webhook server stack that receives external HTTP POSTs (via the local axum server), relays cloud trigger firings polled from the cloud orchestrator, and bridges Smee.io SSE streams into the local event bus. Together these three paths let external systems trigger personas regardless of whether the desktop has a public URL.
contexts.name: webhook-ingestion

contexts.description: Domain types for inbound webhook and Smee relay infrastructure: `WebhookLog` captures each incoming webhook delivery with headers, payload, and processing status; `SmeeRelay` stores configuration for proxying GitHub-style webhooks through the Smee.io relay service during local development. Both power the webhook trigger path for persona automation.
contexts.name: webhook-relay-models

contexts.description: Implements the native desktop window chrome: title bar with minimize/maximize/close controls via Tauri, ambient blur layer, docked icon tray, breadcrumb navigation trail, and the hook managing tray state. Provides the outermost frame users see around every screen. Depends on Tauri window APIs and the navigation history store.
contexts.name: window-chrome

contexts.description: Enables importing external automation workflows (n8n, Zapier, Make, GitHub Actions) into the persona system. Detects the source platform from file content, routes to a platform-specific parser, and runs a shared extraction pipeline that outputs a normalized AgentIR (suggested tools, triggers, connectors, and structured prompt). Platform capability definitions (node-type maps, credential consolidation rules, protocol detection) live in platformDefinitions.ts and are consumed by the parsers.
contexts.name: workflow-import-parsers

contexts.description: Background workflow and task execution infrastructure — the workflow runner (multi-step async workflows), task executor (general background job dispatch), bridge-manifest management (tracking active IPC bridges), CLI stderr capture, and the Bun web-dev builder integration.
contexts.name: workflow-infrastructure

contexts.description: Codebase governance scanning — standards ruleset enforcement (linting rules against a configurable standards file), doc-rot detection (stale documentation finder), workspace divergence analysis, workspace harvesting (extracting structure from managed repos), and Git checkpoint/GitLab integration.
contexts.name: workspace-governance

contexts.description: The Workspaces Knowledge Center organises practices and knowledge across a portfolio of workspaces. WorkspacesAtlas renders the workspace map; WorkspaceTabs and WorkspacePulse show workspace-level health and tabs; SwitcherBreadcrumb and useWorkspaceSwitch manage the active workspace; MoveToWorkspaceButton and WorkspaceEditMenu handle governance actions; workspaceStore persists active state.
contexts.name: workspace-knowledge

contexts.description: The library health dashboard shown above the knowledge tree. Renders four health pillars (governance, currency, consistency, liquidity) and a weekly digest of governance activity, all derived on the fly from the in-memory item list and adoption matrix. Supports expanding to show per-state activity lists with clickable practice titles.
contexts.name: workspace-pulse-dashboard

contexts.description: Repositories for workspace and project taxonomy — categorizing personas into workspaces, projects, and hierarchical groups. Also covers dev workspaces for the developer tools feature where Athena tracks known code repositories.
contexts.name: workspace-taxonomy-repo

use_cases.description: A persona is run against an input (manual, scheduled, or event-triggered), progressing through the prompt→LLM→tool-call→output pipeline with live stage tracking and result surfacing.
use_cases.name: Agent Execution

use_cases.description: The ambient AI companion proactively nudges users toward next actions, answers in-app questions with contextual explain-in-cockpit overlays, creates goals autonomously, and retains long-term memory across sessions.
use_cases.name: Athena Companion

use_cases.description: Users securely store, manage, and rotate secrets for 130+ third-party connectors using AES-256-GCM encryption, OS keyring integration, and OAuth PKCE flows, with health-check probes validating liveness.
use_cases.name: Credential Vault

use_cases.description: Users wire persona executions to external events — inbound webhooks, GitHub/GitLab events, cron schedules, clipboard changes, file-system watches — with rate limiting, dead-letter inspection, and live event streaming.
use_cases.name: Event-Driven Triggers

use_cases.description: Operators drill into live and historical runs via execution timelines with OpenTelemetry-style span waterfalls, cost/token attribution, SLA evaluation, and aggregated analytics across all agents.
use_cases.name: Execution Observability

use_cases.description: Personas expose their tools as MCP-compatible endpoints for external LLM hosts, connect to SQL databases via natural-language query, and interop with GitLab CI/CD — making each persona addressable from outside the app.
use_cases.name: External Protocol Integration

use_cases.description: Users upload documents that are chunked, embedded via ONNX fastembed, and stored in a local SQLite-vec index, enabling semantic retrieval at execution time to ground agent responses in private data.
use_cases.name: Knowledge Base Ingestion

use_cases.description: Users compose personas into sequential or parallel pipelines on a visual canvas, passing outputs from one agent as inputs to the next, with chain-level failure policies and real-time status propagation.
use_cases.name: Multi-Agent Orchestration

use_cases.description: New users complete a guided onboarding overlay (persona coach, credential intro, appearance) and a step-tracked interactive tour that ends with a successfully executed first agent run.
use_cases.name: Onboarding to First Run

use_cases.description: Users build an AI agent persona from scratch or from a template — defining identity, system prompt, model, connectors, use-case cards, and output assertions — and iterate on it via the multi-tab editor.
use_cases.name: Persona Authoring

use_cases.name: Recipe Playback
